domande.spiegazione: Push: memos, emails, status reports, voicemail. Pull: bulletins, web pages, whiteboards (PMBOK 7, p. 13).

domande.domanda: You have taken over a project with a vendor where scope and requirements have been missed, and miscommunication is common. You set an extremely important meeting with your team and the vendor's team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Speak slowly and clearly to the vendor's team, at a louder volume if necessary.
opzioni.B: Confirm they heard your message, determine whether they agree and identify any nuanced or unintended messages.
opzioni.C: Only communicate with the vendor in writing to have a trail of proof.
opzioni.D: Prepare a claim for the mishandled scope through the procurement team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Volume doesn't improve understanding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quick feedback loops confirm the message was heard, agreed and correctly interpreted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Writing loses tone and body language and is more easily misread.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fix the communication first.

domande.spiegazione: Feedback loops: confirm the message was heard, check agreement, identify nuances (PMBOK 7, p. 13).

domande.domanda: Stakeholders seem engaged, but frequent changes to scope and requirements are causing delays, with issues raised and multiple feedback rounds. You're not sure who or what is causing it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform root cause analysis with the team to brainstorm the problem.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk for the project delay and review responses with the team.
opzioni.C: Review the issue log, risk register and change log for the most frequent requesters, then update your engagement approach for them.
opzioni.D: Ensure the budget has enough contingency reserve for the reviews and delays.

domande.hint: Frequent changes may signal stakeholders who are not aligned. How do you find out who?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but C goes further: it finds the who and acts on it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an issue already happening, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The logs reveal which stakeholders drive the changes, so you can engage them better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't just throw money at it.

domande.spiegazione: Many changes may mean stakeholders aren't engaged/aligned; issue and risk registers reveal challenges with individual stakeholders (PMBOK 7, p. 15).

domande.domanda: A manager leads in a dictatorship style; the team has stopped making suggestions, sick days have increased and work has slowed. You suggest servant leadership. What will they do next?

opzioni.A: Serve the team as much as possible, ensuring their every need is met.
opzioni.B: Focus on obstacle removal, encouragement and development opportunities.
opzioni.C: Ensure team members serve one another and help each other succeed.
opzioni.D: Serve the team new ways of doing the work and engage them through variety.

domande.hint: Servant leadership = removing blockers and growing people.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds good, but servant leaders don't meet every need.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Obstacle removal, diversion shielding, encouragement and development are servant leadership behaviors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but not servant leadership specifically.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Right keywords, wrong meaning.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leaders enable self-organization and autonomy, remove obstacles, shield the team and offer development (PMBOK 7, p. 18).

domande.domanda: You have been allocated to a new team with members from different functional areas, few of whom have worked on a project before. Miscommunication and rework are causing delays. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set a daily stand-up so they update what they completed.
opzioni.B: Review the resource assignment matrix to ensure they are doing their job.
opzioni.C: Help the team set its vision and objectives, roles and responsibilities, and team operations.
opzioni.D: Send team members on training in their roles.

domande.hint: A newly formed team needs clarity first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Could help, but doesn't create shared clarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Could help, but is control rather than team development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Vision, roles and ways of working (e.g. a team charter) build a one-team mindset.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the issue is alignment, not individual skill.

domande.spiegazione: Teams formed across organizations need upfront work: shared vision, clear roles, ways of working (PMBOK 7, p. 18).

domande.domanda: You are nearing the end of a difficult project where the vendor took longer than expected. The deliverables have been tested, validated and verified, and the sponsor is keen to close the project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project management plan and approved change requests.
opzioni.B: Review the requirements management plan and requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.C: Review the procurement agreement and the accepted deliverables.
opzioni.D: Review any outstanding risks and issues.

domande.hint: Closing a project that involved a vendor: which inputs matter?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the key inputs for closing here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The requirements management plan is about managing requirements, not closing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Procurement agreements and accepted deliverables are inputs to Close Project or Phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Everything is already tested and accepted.

domande.spiegazione: Inputs to Close Project or Phase include accepted deliverables and procurement agreements (PMBOK 6, p. 124).
domande.nota: Order of options reconstructed from the transcript (the instructor states C and explains the procurement answer).

domande.domanda: Your team is new, inexperienced and lacks capability, and the steering committee pressures you to improve performance. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use Tuckman's ladder (forming, storming, norming, performing) with your team.
opzioni.B: Use co-location, a shared knowledge portal, training and team assessments.
opzioni.C: Use conflict management, influencing and emotional intelligence to get the team on side.
opzioni.D: Use brainstorming and root cause analysis to get to the heart of the problem.

domande.hint: Develop Team tools and techniques for raising capability.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Tuckman is a model of team stages, not a capability tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Co-location, communication technology, training and team assessments are Develop Team tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good skills, but not targeted at capability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the cause (inexperience) is already known.

domande.spiegazione: Develop Team: co-location, interpersonal skills, communication technology, training, team assessments, recognition (PMBOK 6, pp. 340-342).

domande.domanda: You have planned scope, schedule, cost and resources and identified many risks. While assigning probability and impact, one of the risks occurs and the sponsor fears the worst. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use the management reserve to mitigate the risk.
opzioni.B: Review or create the risk response in the risk register, then use the appropriate contingency reserve to implement it.
opzioni.C: Perform quantitative analysis on the risk to know how much it will cost.
opzioni.D: Accept the risk for now, since the risk analysis isn't complete.

domande.hint: An identified risk is a known unknown: which reserve?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Management reserve is for unforeseen in-scope work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Identified risks are covered by contingency reserves through the planned response.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Quantitative analysis is deeper financial analysis, not a response.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A response is still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Known risks go in the risk register with responses; contingency reserves cover known unknowns (PMBOK 6, p. 440).

domande.domanda: A significant scope change is needed after a serious system flaw was found, affecting scope, cost and schedule. You have analyzed the impacts, raised an issue and are about to raise a change request. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the configuration management plan for the baselined items.
opzioni.B: Add the detail as a delivery risk in the risk register.
opzioni.C: Update the change log and implement the changes.
opzioni.D: Check the change management plan for the CCB members and process.

domande.hint: Who approves, and through which process?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You already know it needs change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It has already happened: it's an issue, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't implement before approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The change management plan defines the process and the CCB's roles.

domande.spiegazione: The CCB reviews, approves, defers or rejects changes; the change management plan documents the process and CCB roles (PMBOK 6, p. 116).

domande.domanda: Five major defects found in testing changed scope significantly. You raised change requests; the CCB approved 2, rejected 2 and deferred 1. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Record the outcomes in the change log and communicate the deferred and rejected changes to the requesters.
opzioni.B: Reprioritize the scope to fit the must-have items into delivery.
opzioni.C: Raise a risk for the changes.
opzioni.D: Raise a claim on the affected changes to improve their chance of approval.

domande.hint: After CCB decisions: record and communicate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. All outcomes go in the change log; deferred/rejected ones are communicated to the requester.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changes still go through the change process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It has already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Claims are for contested vendor changes.

domande.spiegazione: Outcomes of all change requests are recorded in the change log; rejected/deferred are communicated to requesters (PMBOK 6, p. 120).

domande.domanda: On a newly started project, the senior user is unsure how requirements and scope come together into a deliverable. Your program manager suggests decomposition. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Estimate activity resources for who is required to deliver the item.
opzioni.B: Define a project scope for the functional manager.
opzioni.C: Create a work breakdown structure and define the activities in the schedule.
opzioni.D: Create the project charter and project management plan.

domande.hint: Decomposition is a tool of which processes?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's not decomposition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Defining scope isn't decomposition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Decomposition is a tool of Create WBS and Define Activities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good documents, but not decomposition.

domande.spiegazione: Decomposition breaks work into smaller, manageable parts; used in Create WBS and Define Activities (PMBOK 6, pp. 156, 185).

domande.domanda: You take over a project with scope creep increasing schedule and cost. You can't understand the team's cadence and way of working, so you want to find their development approach, including modifications. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project charter.
opzioni.B: Review the schedule management plan.
opzioni.C: Review the project management plan.
opzioni.D: Review the stakeholder register.

domande.hint: Where is the development approach documented?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The charter is high-level authorization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It covers the deliverables' schedule, not the team's cadence.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The development approach (predictive, iterative, agile, hybrid) is in the project management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The register lists stakeholders and their needs.

domande.spiegazione: The development approach and modifications are part of the project management plan (PMBOK 6, p. 88).

domande.domanda: On a complex engineering project with many risks, the functional manager wants to work with your team to plan risk responses. You agree to help her update the risk register with:

opzioni.A: Risk triggers, agreed response strategies and residual risks after mitigation.
opzioni.B: Contingency reserves, quantitative analysis and financial impact responses.
opzioni.C: The list of risks, their probability and impact and overall risk rating.
opzioni.D: Risk owners, assumptions and mitigations.

domande.hint: What does Plan Risk Responses add to the register?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Plan Risk Responses adds agreed strategies, triggers (warning signs) and expected residual risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's quantitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's qualitative assessment, not responses.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close, but A is directly about responses.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Risk Responses updates the risk register with strategies, triggers and residual risks (PMBOK 6, p. 448).

domande.domanda: Your project is nearing completion. The sponsor worries she won't know whether the product has the desired effect on her area after release. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Consult the quality management plan.
opzioni.B: Consult the benefits management plan and act according to that process.
opzioni.C: Consult the business case.
opzioni.D: Consult the risk register.

domande.hint: Is the sponsor asking about quality, or business value?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's about testing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The benefits management plan describes how and when benefits are delivered and measured.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The business case explains why, not how benefits are measured.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Risks aren't the point here.

domande.spiegazione: The benefits management plan defines how benefits are delivered and measured; reviewed at closing (PMBOK 6, p. 125).

domande.domanda: Your high-profile software project needs automation technology the company has never used, and you have no resources for it. The steering committee approves outsourcing to a suitable vendor. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform a make-or-buy analysis to ensure a correct decision.
opzioni.B: Ask the procurement department for a suitable contract, such as cost plus incentive fee.
opzioni.C: Create the procurement statement of work and the source selection criteria.
opzioni.D: Review current agreements and change requests impacting third-party work.

domande.hint: The buy decision is already made: what comes next in Plan Procurement Management?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Make-or-buy is already decided.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but it comes after the SOW and selection criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The procurement SOW and source selection criteria are outputs of Plan Procurement Management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No agreements exist yet.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Procurement Management outputs: procurement SOW, source selection criteria, bid documents, procurement strategy (PMBOK 6, pp. 464, 477-478).

domande.domanda: In the initial phase, you are drafting a document for stakeholders to approve the project and decide to apply the 5 Cs of communication. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Connect each part of the communication.
opzioni.B: Create a bond between message sender and receiver.
opzioni.C: Ensure clear purpose and expression directed to the needs of the reader.
opzioni.D: Care about the subject and the person.

domande.hint: 5 Cs of written communication: correct, concise, clear, coherent, controlling.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Clear purpose and expression directed to the reader's needs is one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.

domande.spiegazione: 5 Cs: correct grammar and spelling, concise expression, clear purpose, coherent flow, controlling flow of words and ideas (PMBOK 6, p. 363).

domande.domanda: Communication with stakeholders has grown tense. An engagement assessment shows most are resistant or neutral. What will you NOT do next?

opzioni.A: Ensure you actively listen in each interaction.
opzioni.B: Increase your awareness of cultural and personal differences.
opzioni.C: Identify, set and manage stakeholder expectations.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to their functional manager to bring them back in line.

domande.hint: NOT question: three answers support the 5 Cs, one doesn't.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (you would do it). Active listening supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (you would do it). Cultural awareness supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (you would do it). Managing expectations supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (you would NOT do it). Escalation is a last resort; work with them first.

domande.spiegazione: Skills supporting the 5 Cs: active listening, cultural awareness, managing expectations, negotiation/coaching/conflict skills (PMBOK 6, p. 363).

domande.domanda: On a database transfer project, the data manager identifies aging systems as a threat. You decide with the team to perform qualitative risk analysis. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the quality of the data.
opzioni.B: Assign a probability of occurrence and an impact to the threat.
opzioni.C: Perform analysis on a range of outcomes.
opzioni.D: Add a risk trigger, mitigation and owner to the threat.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the core of qualitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Qualitative analysis prioritizes risks by probability and impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Range of outcomes/simulations is quantitative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Plan Risk Responses.

domande.spiegazione: Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis: prioritize risks by probability and impact (PMBOK 6, p. 419).

domande.domanda: A small process-improvement project has limited resources and budget. Planning risk management, you can't complete every risk task. Which step will you remove?

opzioni.A: Qualitative risk analysis.
opzioni.B: Quantitative risk analysis.
opzioni.C: Identify risks.
opzioni.D: Plan risk management.

domande.hint: Which step costs the most and is mainly for large or complex projects?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Probability and impact are the backbone of risk analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quantitative analysis takes extra time and cost and suits large or strategic projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Risks must still be identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Planning risk management is still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Quantitative risk analysis is not required on every project; most appropriate for large/complex/strategic ones (PMBOK 6, p. 429).

domande.domanda: On a waterfall project, requirements, scope and schedule are planned. You now create the cost estimates. What will you NOT include?

opzioni.A: Contingency amounts for identified risks.
opzioni.B: Known cost of project changes and of managing project change.
opzioni.C: Indirect costs at the activity level, if included in the project estimate.
opzioni.D: Management reserve for unforeseen scope changes.

domande.hint: NOT question: three items belong in the cost estimates.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (included). Contingency for identified risks is included.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (not included). Managing change is part of normal project management, not a cost estimate line.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (included). Indirect costs are included if part of the project estimate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (included, per the source). The management reserve for unforeseen scope is added on top.

domande.spiegazione: Per the source, cost estimates include contingency and management reserves and indirect costs if included in the estimate (PMBOK 6, p. 246).

domande.domanda: You have just taken over a difficult waterfall project. Several stakeholders ask for changes to scope, cost and schedule. You need to know which items need change approval and which can just be done. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the change management plan.
opzioni.B: Review the scope management plan.
opzioni.C: Review the configuration management plan for baselined items.
opzioni.D: Review the requirements traceability matrix.

domande.hint: Which plan lists items under configuration control?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It explains the change process, not which items are baselined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It covers how scope is managed, not which items are baselined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The configuration management plan identifies baselined items that need change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It links requirements to scope.

domande.spiegazione: Configuration management plan = which items are baselined; change management plan = how changes are processed (PMBOK 6, p. 169).
domande.nota: Order of options reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: You are new to a project. A functional manager says no one has told them what the project is about: high-level scope, schedule, risks and who approved it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Check the project activity list and schedule.
opzioni.B: Hold a sprint review to see what the team has developed.
opzioni.C: Review the project charter and identify the stakeholders impacted by the change.
opzioni.D: Visit the PMO to gather organizational process assets.

domande.hint: Which document holds the high-level summary of the project?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No risks or approvals there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Only shows an increment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The charter contains purpose, high-level requirements, milestones, risks, stakeholders and the approver.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. OPAs are too generic.

domande.spiegazione: The charter holds the high-level information to get up to speed (PMBOK 6, p. 155).

domande.domanda: The previous PM left and you're finishing a nearly complete project. Deliverables are accepted; you need to communicate the release to all affected stakeholders in the way they agreed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the communications management plan.
opzioni.B: Review the stakeholder engagement plan.
opzioni.C: Review the stakeholder register.
opzioni.D: Review the resource management plan.

domande.hint: Where are the agreed communication requirements?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. It describes how communications are planned, structured, implemented and monitored, including stakeholder requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. More about engagement than communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Lists who, not how.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. About project resources.

domande.spiegazione: Communications management plan: stakeholder communication requirements, information, reasons, methods (PMBOK 6, p. 377).

domande.domanda: The sponsor adds a new executive to the working group. As soon as they arrive, they raise a new scope item not in the original plan. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a change request to change the scope baseline.
opzioni.B: Update the stakeholder register with the new stakeholder's details.
opzioni.C: Raise an issue for the scope change in the issue log.
opzioni.D: Update the change log with initial details of the scope change.

domande.hint: A new stakeholder has just joined: what comes first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Analyze first: you don't know if the change is valid.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Add and analyze the new stakeholder first (role, influence, requirements).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Possibly later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possibly later.

domande.spiegazione: The stakeholder register holds identification, assessment and classification info; update it when a stakeholder joins (PMBOK 6, p. 514).

domande.domanda: Your team complains about poor stakeholder engagement in part of the organization. It now impacts the schedule and you may need contingency reserve to crash it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the cost management plan and access the contingency reserve.
opzioni.B: Perform root cause analysis on the problem with your team.
opzioni.C: Raise the engagement as a risk and escalate it to the functional manager.
opzioni.D: Change to agile to increase stakeholder engagement.

domande.hint: Solve the problem before spending money.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't spend reserves before analyzing the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Find the root cause first; use reserves only if necessary.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's already happening, and escalation isn't first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile is not a silver bullet.

domande.spiegazione: Root cause analysis identifies causes for problem solving (PMBOK 6, p. 292).

domande.domanda: Delivering a new product line partly on a third-party system, the functional manager warns the system is being discontinued and losing support within 12 months. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Update the risk register.
opzioni.B: Ignore the concern.
opzioni.C: Escalate the concern to the sponsor.
opzioni.D: Update the issue log.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. It's a future uncertain event: record it in the risk register.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never ignore concerns.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Own it first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It hasn't happened yet.

domande.spiegazione: Risks can be identified at any time and recorded in the risk register (PMBOK 6, p. 409).

domande.domanda: You've joined a car manufacturer as a new PM. Senior management asks you to take the steps needed to kick-start a project for a new electronic dashboard. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review marketplace conditions.
opzioni.B: Create a cost-benefit analysis and feasibility study for a business case.
opzioni.C: Gather the high-level requirements, scope, milestones and risks for a project charter.
opzioni.D: Start the project with a kickoff meeting and begin gathering resources.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possibly useful, but doesn't start the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but the charter is what kick-starts it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Develop Project Charter is the first initiating step and authorizes using resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too early without a charter.

domande.spiegazione: The charter formally authorizes the project and gives the PM authority to use resources (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 81).

domande.domanda: The team has just defined the scope and matched it to requirements in the RTM, but can't agree on what to do next. What will you ask them to do?

opzioni.A: Ask the quality team to verify the scope.
opzioni.B: Ask the sponsor to accept the project scope.
opzioni.C: Break the scope into activities and place them on the schedule.
opzioni.D: Review the scope management plan for direction on creating the WBS.

domande.hint: Order: collect requirements, define scope, create WBS.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Quality verifies deliverables later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Acceptance comes much later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Scheduling comes after the WBS.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Next is Create WBS, as directed by the scope management plan.

domande.spiegazione: Scope order: collect requirements, define scope, create WBS; the scope management plan describes how (PMBOK 6, pp. 130, 137).

domande.domanda: You take over a project halfway through that has used 75% of its budget. A feature change is requested after UAT and the team can't agree whether changes should be made at all. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Check the change management plan for how to make changes.
opzioni.B: Check the RTM for how requirements should be traced.
opzioni.C: Blame the previous PM for not having a process.
opzioni.D: Check the scope management plan for how scope is managed.

domande.hint: The question is whether to change at all, not how.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Close, but it explains how to change, not whether scope can change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not about a change decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Take responsibility.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The scope management plan says how scope is defined, validated, monitored and controlled.

domande.spiegazione: Scope management plan: how scope is defined, validated, monitored and controlled (PMBOK 6, p. 169).
domande.nota: The instructor considers A and D very close.

domande.domanda: On a process improvement, a developer will automate the process once streamlined. They must understand the process thoroughly, including criteria to test the automation. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gather your team and the developer and create a flowchart together.
opzioni.B: Create an affinity diagram.
opzioni.C: Perform a cost-benefit analysis for the automation.
opzioni.D: Create a quality management plan.

domande.hint: Which tool shows a process step by step?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A flowchart shows the process start to finish with decision points and participants.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Groups similar ideas.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't explain the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Describes how quality is managed.

domande.spiegazione: Flowcharts show a process with decision points and actors; a Plan Quality tool (PMBOK 6, p. 282).

domande.domanda: Design, scope and cost are planned upfront, but part of the project relies on a vendor's new add-on that will undergo many changes. Which life cycle will you recommend?

opzioni.A: Predictive (waterfall).
opzioni.B: Iterative.
opzioni.C: Incremental.
opzioni.D: Hybrid, combining pre-planned activities with iterations and ceremonies for the changeable parts.

domande.hint: Some parts are fixed, some are evolving.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't handle the changing part.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. One release refined over iterations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Delivers increments but doesn't fit the upfront planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Hybrid: predictive for known parts, adaptive for evolving parts.

domande.spiegazione: Hybrid life cycle combines predictive and adaptive elements (PMBOK 6, p. 19).

domande.domanda: Your project has created the scope baseline. The sponsor wants to know how much the scope will cost. What is the next best action?

opzioni.A: Create the project budget.
opzioni.B: Define and sequence the activities and estimate their durations.
opzioni.C: Create the resource management plan.
opzioni.D: Review the project charter for high-level scope, schedule and costs.

domande.hint: You can't cost what you haven't scheduled.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The budget needs activities, durations and resources first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Next is defining activities, sequencing and estimating durations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the next step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You're past initiation.

domande.spiegazione: Budget requires activities, durations and resources (PMBOK 6, p. 174).

domande.domanda: Drafting a charter for a new data system, you ask the internal enterprise data team for an estimate, but the sponsor thinks a vendor would provide the best solution. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the charter and let the steering committee decide.
opzioni.B: Perform a make-or-buy analysis with a payback.
opzioni.C: Ask the data team for their lowest quote to ensure they win.
opzioni.D: Take an agile approach and deliver in increments.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You need the analysis first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Make-or-buy with payback compares initial and ongoing costs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. May lead to cutting corners.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't answer make or buy.

domande.spiegazione: Make-or-buy may include payback, NPV, cost-benefit analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 473).

domande.domanda: A functional manager unhappy with the changes argues constantly, misses meetings and demands multiple sign-offs. The sponsor asks for a win-win approach. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Smooth and accommodate, emphasizing areas of agreement.
opzioni.B: Collaborate and problem-solve with the manager.
opzioni.C: Compromise and reconcile with the manager.
opzioni.D: Force and direct the manager.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Smoothing is lose-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Collaborate/problem solve is the only win-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Compromise is lose-lose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Forcing is win-lose.

domande.spiegazione: Conflict: smooth = lose-win; compromise = lose-lose; force = win-lose; collaborate = win-win (PMBOK 6, p. 348).

domande.domanda: On a large multi-year project, estimates from a year ago are inaccurate and the project is off track. You want an approach giving a high-level view of future work and a detailed view of near-term work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Recommend a decomposition approach.
opzioni.B: Recommend the process in the schedule management plan.
opzioni.C: Recommend an iterative development approach.
opzioni.D: Recommend rolling wave planning.

domande.hint: Detailed near term, high-level far term.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Decomposition breaks down work but isn't this approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You're trying to change that process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. About refining a single release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Rolling wave plans near-term work in detail, future work at a high level.

domande.spiegazione: Rolling wave planning (PMBOK 6, p. 185).

domande.domanda: In the initiating stage at a car manufacturer losing market share to high fuel prices, you are asked to build a business case outlining options, and specifically to perform benchmarking. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Find which competitor products have been benchmarked for future production.
opzioni.B: Compare the specifications of popular fuel-efficient cars on the market with your products.
opzioni.C: Create a project charter to use as a benchmark for your future project management plan.
opzioni.D: Benchmark your current scope, cost and schedule to use as values for project performance.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A wordplay trap; not benchmarking.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Comparing your products with comparable ones on the market is benchmarking.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wordplay trap: a charter isn't a benchmark.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's baselining, not benchmarking.

domande.spiegazione: Benchmarking compares products, processes and practices with comparable organizations (PMBOK 6, p. 143).

domande.domanda: Reviewing project performance: Activity A is on the critical path and delayed 5 days; Activity B is not on the critical path and delayed 7 days; Activity C is on the critical path and delayed 3 days; Activity D is not on the critical path and delayed 2 days. In which order should the team focus its efforts?

opzioni.A: B, A, C, D
opzioni.B: A, B, C, D
opzioni.C: A, C, B, D
opzioni.D: C, A, D, B

domande.hint: Critical path first, then the biggest delays.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. B is not on the critical path, so it doesn't come first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. C (critical path) must come before B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Critical path activities first (A then C, by delay), then the others by delay (B then D).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Among critical activities, A is more delayed than C.

domande.spiegazione: Address critical path tasks first, then the most delayed (PMBOK 6, p. 210).
domande.nota: Delay values for B, C and D and the option sequences are reconstructed: the transcript only gives A (critical, 5 days) and the answer order A, C, B, D.

domande.domanda: Most analysts, developers and testers are unfamiliar with the system they'll modify. The sponsor asks you to address this potential future quality issue with training sessions and their associated cost. What type of cost is this?

opzioni.A: Appraisal cost.
opzioni.B: Prevention cost.
opzioni.C: Internal failure cost.
opzioni.D: Sunk cost.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Appraisal is auditing/checking work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Training prevents future quality issues: prevention cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Defects caught before release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Money already spent.

domande.spiegazione: Cost of quality: prevention, appraisal, internal and external failure (PMBOK 6, p. 282).

domande.domanda: Planning is finished, baselines approved, and the team has planned and estimated activity resources. The team is ready to begin execution. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Define with the team how to estimate, acquire, manage and use team and physical resources.
opzioni.B: Estimate team resources and the type and quantities of materials, equipment and supplies.
opzioni.C: Obtain team members, facilities, equipment, materials, supplies and other resources.
opzioni.D: Monitor planned versus actual resource utilization and take corrective action.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's Plan Resource Management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's Estimate Activity Resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Acquire Resources is the next step, in execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Control Resources, later.

domande.spiegazione: Acquire Resources: obtaining team members, facilities, equipment, materials (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 328).

domande.domanda: On a large waterfall project, a business analyst wants to take on higher duties and move into project management. What advice will you give?

opzioni.A: Work on soft skills: communication, conflict management and negotiation.
opzioni.B: Ensure they can create a project charter and project management plan.
opzioni.C: Work on technical project management, leadership, and strategic and business management skills.
opzioni.D: Work on contracts and procurement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Important, but only part of the picture.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Can be taught with templates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The Talent Triangle: technical PM, leadership, strategic and business management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only a small part of PM.

domande.spiegazione: PMI Talent Triangle (PMBOK 6, p. 56).

domande.domanda: A new PMO advises PMs to fulfill their roles within their sphere of influence. What is your responsibility toward the organization?

opzioni.A: Proactively interact with other PMs on demands for the same resources, funding and alignment of project goals with the organization.
opzioni.B: Communicate within your project.
opzioni.C: Understand changing market niches and standards.
opzioni.D: Educate other professionals about the value of project management.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Working with other PMs on resources, funding and alignment is the organizational sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's the project sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's the industry sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's across disciplines.

domande.spiegazione: PM's sphere of influence (PMBOK 6, p. 52).

domande.domanda: You have just joined an organization and are about to be allocated to a behind-schedule, $40,000-over-budget HR system project with many stakeholders. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a project management plan outlining processes for each phase.
opzioni.B: Perform a stakeholder engagement assessment to see who is sabotaging the project.
opzioni.C: Start by understanding how the organization works, including its politics and power.
opzioni.D: Meet the sponsor to understand why the project is off track.

domande.hint: You're new to the organization and not yet assigned.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An existing project already has a plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not assigned yet; stakeholders aren't first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Understand the enterprise environmental factors: how work actually gets done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor doesn't manage the project.

domande.spiegazione: Understand internal EEFs, politics and power (PMBOK 6, p. 62).

domande.domanda: You must manage a large multi-department change and staff the team with people with strong leadership skills. What will you NOT look for?

opzioni.A: People who build trust, balance opposing goals and apply persuasion and conflict resolution.
opzioni.B: People who give and accept feedback constructively.
opzioni.C: People who can describe the product, goals and objectives of the project.
opzioni.D: People who ensure the work is done their way to get the fastest result.

domande.hint: NOT question: which isn't a leadership quality?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (look for it). Trust and conflict resolution are leader skills.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (look for it). Feedback is a leader skill.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (look for it). Communicating the vision is a leader skill.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (NOT). A 'my way' dictatorship isn't good leadership.

domande.spiegazione: Leader qualities: integrity, vision, collaboration, appropriate influence (PMBOK 6, p. 61).

domande.domanda: You're a junior PM on an internal process improvement within your existing team. Your manager asks you to use the forms of power available to you. Which is best?

opzioni.A: Situational power.
opzioni.B: Positional power.
opzioni.C: Coercive power.
opzioni.D: Informational power.

domande.hint: Junior, no position, but you know your team's process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're not in a situation granting power.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You have no formal position.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't discipline or reward.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. You hold information and expert judgment from your own team.

domande.spiegazione: Forms of power (PMBOK 6, p. 63).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the transcript names the four types but not the answer letter.

domande.domanda: On a waterfall project, several tasks are falling behind but are not on the critical path and have several days of float, so you can adjust their dates without affecting the project. Which technique will you use?

opzioni.A: Resource smoothing.
opzioni.B: Schedule crashing.
opzioni.C: Schedule fast tracking.
opzioni.D: Resource leveling.

domande.hint: Using existing float without moving the end date.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Smoothing uses available float without changing the critical path/end date.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Adds money and resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Runs activities in parallel.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Leveling can extend the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: Resource optimization (PMBOK 6, p. 211).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: A third of your team worked on a similar project. Requirements and high-level scope are done; now you must estimate size and effort, but the customer wants progress quickly. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the customer to wait so you can plan properly.
opzioni.B: Estimate using parametric estimating.
opzioni.C: Break the scope into smaller parts with a WBS.
opzioni.D: Estimate using analogous estimating.

domande.hint: Quick estimate from a similar past project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Serve the customer instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Uses a unit rate; not the clue here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Needed later, but you're asked to estimate now.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Analogous estimating uses similar past projects and is fast.

domande.spiegazione: Analogous estimating (PMBOK 6, p. 324).

domande.domanda: You've been asked to monitor changes to a product before completing the next phase. Reviewing the control chart, the data is within the upper and lower control limits, with an upward trend of four data points and six points above the average line. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the next phase, as the process is in control.
opzioni.B: Delay the next phase and rework the current release, as the process is out of control.
opzioni.C: Ask the sponsor to validate the released deliverable.
opzioni.D: Proceed with quality testing to verify the created deliverables.

domande.hint: Rule of seven: 7+ points on one side of the mean, 5+ in a trend, or any point outside the limits.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Only 4 points trending and 6 above the mean, all within limits: the process is in control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. None of the out-of-control rules is triggered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor: the question is about reading the control chart, not validation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor: verification isn't what the control chart asks you to decide.

domande.spiegazione: Control chart rules: out of control if 7+ points on one side, 5+ in one direction, or any point outside the limits (Green Belt Handbook, p. 404).

domande.domanda: You are planning the resources for your project. Work hasn't started because the team is not sure what they should be doing. You decide to create the resource management plan with them. What output do you specifically need from this plan?

opzioni.A: The stakeholder register.
opzioni.B: The project charter.
opzioni.C: The requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.D: Roles and responsibilities, with role details, authority and competence.

domande.hint: The team doesn't know what to do: which output tells them?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It captures people involved in the project, not team roles and responsibilities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The charter already exists and initiates the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It traces requirements to scope, not resources to work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Roles and responsibilities (role, authority, competence) is the specific output that clarifies who does what.

domande.spiegazione: Resource management plan: roles and responsibilities, with role, authority and competence (PMBOK 6, p. 318).

domande.domanda: An external quality assurance manager executed the quality management plan with her testing team and found a high number of low-impact defects. You need to see where the biggest impacts actually are. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use a histogram.
opzioni.B: Use a flowchart.
opzioni.C: Use a matrix diagram.
opzioni.D: Use an affinity diagram.

domande.hint: You need to count occurrences per category.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A histogram is a bar chart counting items (here defects) per category, showing the most common.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A flowchart shows the steps of a process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A matrix diagram shows relationships between groups of factors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An affinity diagram groups similar ideas.

domande.spiegazione: Histograms show the frequency of items per category (PMBOK 6, p. 293).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads flowchart, matrix, affinity and histogram, then answers A.

domande.domanda: Your new team comes from many parts of the organization, each with its own agenda. There are many small conflicts and little work is getting done. The program manager asks you to use your positional power to resolve these conflicts while the team finds its rhythm. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Withdraw from the conflicts.
opzioni.B: Force a decision on the conflicts.
opzioni.C: Smooth and accommodate all sides in the conflicts.
opzioni.D: Problem-solve the conflicts with the team.

domande.hint: Positional power and a need for quick results.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Withdrawing doesn't resolve anything.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Forcing uses positional power to resolve conflicts quickly (win-lose), at the cost of other benefits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Smoothing doesn't use positional power and doesn't fit the urgency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Second best: collaboration is ideal but takes more time than you have here.

domande.spiegazione: Forcing/directing: pushing a viewpoint at the expense of others; resolves conflicts quickly (PMBOK 6, p. 349).

domande.domanda: During your project, the company was taken over by a larger company and the PMO and its policies changed. The customer has already formally accepted the deliverables, delivery is complete and the project is ready to be closed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Refer to the project charter for the closing procedures.
opzioni.B: Refer to the scope management plan for the acceptance of deliverables.
opzioni.C: Gather the details of the accepted deliverables, agreements and procurement documentation to close the project.
opzioni.D: The project can't be closed, as the project outcomes need to be measured and accepted.

domande.hint: Which inputs do you need to close the project?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The charter initiates the project; closing procedures aren't there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Acceptance has already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Accepted deliverables, agreements and procurement documentation are inputs to Close Project or Phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Outcomes can be measured after the project, and deliverables are already accepted.

domande.spiegazione: Close Project or Phase inputs: accepted deliverables, agreements, procurement documentation (PMBOK 6, p. 126).

domande.domanda: A highly influential stakeholder raises an urgent change to be implemented within two weeks. The change management plan says changes can be approved by the project manager. You raised a change request and reviewed the impact on schedule and cost. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the configuration management plan to see which documents are baselined.
opzioni.B: Review the schedule and earned value reports for your project.
opzioni.C: Decide on the changes, approve them and track them.
opzioni.D: Review the RTM for requirement acceptance and sign-off.

domande.hint: In this project, you are the approver.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're past that stage: you already know it needs a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Already done: that was the impact review.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Since the PM can approve, the next steps are decide, approve and track the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not related to the change decision.

domande.spiegazione: EV reports are inputs to change control; with impact known, the approver decides, approves and tracks (PMBOK 6, p. 119).

domande.domanda: You're measuring the outcome of one of your deliverables on the business. The data shows an improvement, but the range of results is very wide, while you can get very clear individual results. Based on this, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Low accuracy and high precision: the measuring equipment should be recalibrated.
opzioni.B: Low accuracy and high precision: the deliverable process should be improved.
opzioni.C: High accuracy and low precision: the measuring equipment should be recalibrated.
opzioni.D: High accuracy and low precision: the deliverable process should be improved.

domande.hint: Wide range = low accuracy; very clear results = high precision.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The diagnosis is right, but precision is already good, so measurement isn't the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Results are precise but scattered: improve the process to narrow the range.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Accuracy is low (wide range), not high.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Accuracy is low and precision is high, not the opposite.

domande.spiegazione: Low accuracy = large range; precision = how exact the outcome is (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: Over the last few months your team had a lot of conflict finding their roles. They are now starting to work together and adjust their habits and behaviors to support the team. As a leader, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Help the team work through the storming stage.
opzioni.B: Take the team back to the forming stage.
opzioni.C: Help the team use the norming stage to move into performing.
opzioni.D: Move the team to the adjourning stage.

domande.hint: Tuckman: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The conflict (storming) is already behind them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team has already formed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adjusting behaviors to support the team is norming: help them move into performing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Adjourning happens when the team is released at the end.

domande.spiegazione: Tuckman ladder (PMBOK 6, p. 338).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: You used the project charter and statement to create the project management plan. Presenting it to key stakeholders, including the sponsor, you sense strong dissatisfaction from the customer's executives, who don't believe the project will produce the results they expected. What should you do next?

opzioni.A: Request a written statement from the customer detailing their concerns.
opzioni.B: Proceed as normal: your plan will produce a convincing product.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request, replan where necessary and go ahead with the work.
opzioni.D: Work together with the customer to create a narrative scope statement outlining the deliverables.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Writing is tempting, but talking together resolves it better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Proceeding with unconvinced executives will cause problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You don't yet know what the dissatisfaction is about.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Defining the scope statement (description, deliverables, acceptance criteria) together aligns expectations.

domande.spiegazione: Collaborative approach plus the proper Define Scope output: the scope statement (PMBOK 6, p. 154).

domande.domanda: You have planned, executed and monitored a project to completion. The customer has received the product but says they're unhappy, that your team didn't listen to their quality concerns, and they are raising a claim against your company. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a change request for their proposed changes and update the project plan.
opzioni.B: Call their bluff, take the claim to dispute and appeal if necessary.
opzioni.C: Review the claims process in the contract and negotiate with them to settle the claim.
opzioni.D: Review the earned value report for any impact on schedule and cost.

domande.hint: What is the preferred way to handle claims?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project is essentially finished; this is a claim, not a change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Disputes and litigation are a last resort.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Follow the contract's claims process and settle through negotiation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too late to be useful, and it doesn't address the claim.

domande.spiegazione: Claims administration: the claims process is in the contract; negotiation is the preferred settlement (PMBOK 6, p. 498).

domande.domanda: You're creating a project charter to gain resources for an automated process improvement. The sponsor, who is also the functional manager of those resources, rejects it: it lists everything you want from her team but nothing about what her area gets in return. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Rework the charter to include the benefits management plan and success measures.
opzioni.B: Escalate the charter to the sponsor's manager, as the project is important.
opzioni.C: Ask the sponsor to work agile and start delivering an MVP.
opzioni.D: Begin the requirements management plan to show how her requirements will be tracked.

domande.hint: She needs to see the value for her area.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Benefits, strategic alignment and success measures (ROI, payback) show what she gets.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Escalation is a last resort and may not even be available.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can explain the benefits without delivering anything first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That belongs to planning, after the charter is approved.

domande.spiegazione: The charter ideally includes the benefits management plan and success measures (PMBOK 6, pp. 343-344).

domande.domanda: On a complex, high-value project to replace the organization's telecommunication system, you issued an RFQ with source selection criteria and a statement of work, and selected a seller from multiple responses. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Record the new vendor in the stakeholder register and begin engaging them to deliver.
opzioni.B: Draft an appropriate contract, such as fixed price incentive fee, to proceed.
opzioni.C: Place the approved RFQ in the procurement management plan and proceed with delivery.
opzioni.D: Approach organizational senior management for approval to award the contract.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't begin delivery before the award.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Tempting (the instructor picked it), but award approval comes first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't proceed with delivery yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Complex, high-value, high-risk procurements generally need senior management approval before award.

domande.spiegazione: Conduct Procurements outputs: selected sellers; complex procurements need senior approval before award (PMBOK 6, p. 488).
domande.nota: The instructor initially chose B and got it wrong: a classic trap.

domande.domanda: You're planning with a waterfall approach and must estimate resources. The PMO has stopped using third parties or off-site workers and mandates on-site resources only. Reviewing the activity list, you realize some essential resources currently work off-site. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Discuss the available options with the project sponsor.
opzioni.B: Perform alternatives analysis on the impact of both on-site and off-site workers.
opzioni.C: Update the resource management plan with the on-site mandate.
opzioni.D: Update the resource calendar with available people, locations and dates before baselining.

domande.hint: Analyze before discussing or updating plans.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but you need the analysis before the discussion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Alternatives analysis finds the best way to perform the work within the constraints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Comes later, after the options are discussed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Comes last in the sequence.

domande.spiegazione: Estimate Activity Resources, data analysis: alternatives analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 325). Sequence: B, A, C, D.

domande.domanda: The organization wanted only on-site workers, while you believed the project needed off-site skills. You agreed to use on-site workers, but the work isn't being done to specification and you really need the off-site workers. The project is going off track. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Update the issue log and the resource calendar with the resource requirements.
opzioni.B: Use problem solving with your team and negotiation with the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Gather work performance information from the team and raise a change request.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk in the risk register and brainstorm responses with the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Logging the issue is fine but doesn't solve it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Problem solving and negotiation are Control Resources tools to fix it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Change requests are for impacts on baselined items, not yet here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening: it's an issue, not a risk.

domande.spiegazione: Control Resources: problem solving and negotiation (PMBOK 6, pp. 356-357).

domande.domanda: On a critical infrastructure project, your team has 12 months of experience in this area. In a working group meeting they say they're stuck and can't implement part of the project. You log an issue and decide to problem-solve with the team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Escalate the problem outside your team, as they clearly can't move forward.
opzioni.B: Review the lessons learned register for similar past problems.
opzioni.C: Define the problem with data, identify the root cause and generate possible solutions.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to delivery and note its impact and likelihood.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team is experienced; outsiders may complicate things.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but weaker than structured problem solving.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Define with data, find the root cause, generate and choose solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening: it's an issue.

domande.spiegazione: Problem solving: define the problem, find root cause, generate solutions, choose and test (PMBOK 6, pp. 295, 356).

domande.domanda: Your high-level project charter has been approved. The sponsor expects you to start straight away, but you don't know who to approach or who is available to help. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Identify stakeholders with an organizational breakdown chart and include them in your project plan.
opzioni.B: Create a RACI (resource assignment matrix).
opzioni.C: Review and update the resource calendar.
opzioni.D: Review the high-level stakeholders in the charter and begin your project.

domande.hint: After Develop Project Charter comes Identify Stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Identify stakeholders next; an organizational breakdown chart shows who is where.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't assign people you haven't identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too early: you don't know who is involved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The charter's stakeholders are too high-level.

domande.spiegazione: Identify Stakeholders follows the charter (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 316).

domande.domanda: You've been assigned to address fast-moving competition taking market share. The executive says jobs will be lost within 12 months, but there are no projects yet to address it. As project manager, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the executive manager to come up with project ideas.
opzioni.B: Perform benchmarking against various companies for improvement opportunities.
opzioni.C: Create a project charter with high-level scope, milestones and cost for approval.
opzioni.D: Create a business case including the business need, situation analysis and solution options.

domande.hint: What must exist before a charter?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only one input; you have better tools for analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but it feeds the business case and is less complete.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A charter needs a business case first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The business case defines the need, analyzes the situation and proposes options.

domande.spiegazione: Business case comes before the charter (PMBOK 6, pp. 30-31).

domande.domanda: You have just started on a project that has been in development for six months. It has gone through many steps you are unfamiliar with, such as concept development, feasibility study, commissioning and milestone review, which don't match the usual design, build and test phases. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Advise the project to reduce and update its phases for less admin and faster delivery.
opzioni.B: Ask the project to adhere to the normal design, build and test phases as per the guide.
opzioni.C: Adhere to the project's phases and familiarize yourself with the organization's process.
opzioni.D: Remove the phases altogether and work through waterfall delivery with one big release.

domande.hint: You're new: every organization has its own environment (EEFs).

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You've just arrived: don't change the process before understanding it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Phase names vary by organization; imposing the guide's names is dictating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Respect the enterprise environmental factors and learn the organization's practices first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Removing phases is a drastic, dictated change.

domande.spiegazione: Each organization has its own politics, governance and approvals: adhere to the EEFs and learn its practices (PMBOK 6, p. 20).

domande.domanda: The PMO asks you to help hire and coach new project managers and to interview the next candidate. You find the candidate has no industry experience. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask whether they prefer waterfall or agile, to see if they work like your organization.
opzioni.B: Ask whether they would like a different job in the company with less focus on industry experience.
opzioni.C: Ask whether they can dictate and command a team to get fast results.
opzioni.D: Ask what their focus on a project would be: the schedule, selected financial reports or the issue log.

domande.hint: No industry experience doesn't mean no PM skills: test technical project management knowledge.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Methodology labels matter less than understanding the underlying process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Premature: you haven't assessed their PM skills yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Dictatorship gets fast results at the expense of psychological safety and long-term performance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Schedule, financial reports and issue log are the top focuses of leading PMs: this tests technical PM skills.

domande.spiegazione: Talent Triangle: technical PM, business management and leadership skills; leading PMs focus on schedule, financial reports and issue log (PMBOK 6, p. 58).

domande.domanda: Your project charter has been approved and you are gathering the customer requirements. The customer says they have been burned in the past by projects that didn't deliver what they really needed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create an initial list of requirements as part of a solid requirements management plan.
opzioni.B: Call a focus group with the customer's experts and brainstorm requirements with them.
opzioni.C: Perform benchmarking between the area's process and external organizations.
opzioni.D: Create a requirements traceability matrix to ensure requirements are tracked properly.

domande.hint: Want to give the customer what they need? Go to the source.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The requirements management plan is about how requirements are managed; you shouldn't write the list yourself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Direct collaboration through focus groups and brainstorming captures what the customer really needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Benchmarking compares processes; it doesn't gather this customer's needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful for tracking, but first you must collect the requirements from the customer.

domande.spiegazione: Collect Requirements tools: brainstorming, interviews, focus groups, questionnaires, benchmarking (PMBOK 6, p. 138).

domande.domanda: Your deliverables passed quality checks by a specialist testing team. You take them to the sponsor for acceptance, but she accepts all except two: one she notes as a defect and one as a missed requirement. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Make the changes as soon as possible to avoid further delays.
opzioni.B: Raise an issue in the issue log, as this will delay your project.
opzioni.C: Raise change requests for the items, along with the reasons for non-acceptance.
opzioni.D: Proceed as normal, since you delivered as per the project needs.

domande.hint: Waterfall: changes go through checks and balances.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Changes need to go through the change control process first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It may become an issue, but the change request comes first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Deliverables not accepted lead to change requests documenting the reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. They have not been accepted, so you can't ignore them.

domande.spiegazione: Validate Scope outputs: change requests for deliverables not formally accepted, with the reasons (PMBOK 6, p. 166).

domande.domanda: You have gathered the customer requirements with your team and are finishing the scope statement. You need to baseline the project scope so future changes are tracked. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take the scope statement to the sponsor and steering committee for approval.
opzioni.B: Ask the sponsor to approve the project charter and project management plan with the high-level scope.
opzioni.C: Update the configuration management plan with the scope statement as a baselined document.
opzioni.D: Create the work breakdown structure and WBS dictionary with your team.

domande.hint: The scope baseline is more than the scope statement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The scope statement alone isn't the full baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too high-level for a scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The baseline needs more than the scope statement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. With the scope statement done, create the WBS and WBS dictionary to complete the scope baseline.

domande.spiegazione: Scope baseline: scope statement, WBS, WBS dictionary and work packages (PMBOK 6, pp. 161-162).

domande.domanda: On a waterfall project, the team has collected requirements from a customer eager to start. You meet the business analysts to create the scope statement from these requirements. What will you include?

opzioni.A: The scope description, deliverables, acceptance criteria and exclusions.
opzioni.B: The scope description, the WBS and the WBS dictionary.
opzioni.C: The scope management plan, the statement of work and the requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.D: The project charter, the project management plan and the accepted deliverables.

domande.hint: Don't confuse the scope statement with the scope baseline.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. These are the contents of the project scope statement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's the scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. These are other documents (process, procurement, traceability).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Important documents, but not the scope statement contents.

domande.spiegazione: Project scope statement: description, deliverables, acceptance criteria, exclusions (PMBOK 6, p. 154).

domande.domanda: You've been assigned to a project that is behind schedule. Some team members ask what they should be working on. A senior analyst recommends you work together to create the WBS dictionary. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a scope breakdown with unique identifier, description and acceptance criteria.
opzioni.B: Work with the senior analyst to create a resource assignment matrix instead, and coach them on the difference between a RAM and a WBS dictionary.
opzioni.C: Gather the project scope and break it down into smaller work packages.
opzioni.D: Create a scope breakdown with unique identifier, description and resource requirements.

domande.hint: What does the team actually need to know? Who works on what.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's a WBS dictionary: the trap suggested by the analyst.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A RAM shows who is assigned to each work package, answering the team's question.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but doesn't tell people what they should work on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Also a WBS dictionary variant: still not an assignment matrix.

domande.spiegazione: A RAM shows the connections between work packages/activities and team members (PMBOK 6, pp. 162, 317).
domande.nota: Trick question: the instructor warns about it.

domande.domanda: The charter is approved and you've identified the stakeholders. As the project progresses, you notice several stakeholders actively trying to sabotage your project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix and invite feedback from those who are resistant.
opzioni.B: Remove the people who seem to be slowing the project from your project team.
opzioni.C: Escalate the problem to their functional managers for disciplinary action.
opzioni.D: Review the impact/influence matrix to determine how to engage the stakeholders.

domande.hint: Find who is resistant, then engage them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The engagement matrix (unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading) shows who is at risk; then invite their feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You often can't remove stakeholders: you must bring them on board.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Escalation may win their minds but not their hearts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Shows power and impact, not who is resistant.

domande.spiegazione: Assess engagement and gather feedback, then use communication and interpersonal skills (PMBOK 6, pp. 521, 527).

domande.domanda: Your project involves nearly a dozen teams across the country and thousands of impacted stakeholders. Executives in these areas are concerned about the changes and are pushing back on your planning. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the project charter and arrange sign-off by the executives.
opzioni.B: Create the communications management plan to ensure their communication needs are met.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request to co-locate all the teams.
opzioni.D: Create the RTM so you can trace the executives' requirements to the scope and keep them engaged.

domande.hint: The project is already under way: how do you meet their information needs?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project is in progress, so the charter is already approved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The communications management plan addresses stakeholders' communication requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Costly, may not be possible and doesn't address the concerns.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful, but you still need to communicate in the right way.

domande.spiegazione: Communications management plan: stakeholder communication requirements, timely distribution of information (PMBOK 6, p. 377).

domande.domanda: Several risks have been raised. You performed qualitative analysis for a subjective risk rating, but the customer wants additional qualitative analysis beyond impact and likelihood. What will you analyze next?

opzioni.A: Simulation, sensitivity analysis and decision tree analysis.
opzioni.B: Cost of failure, cost of appraisal and cost of prevention.
opzioni.C: Executive needs, political needs and promotion needs.
opzioni.D: Urgency, proximity and strategic impact of the risks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are quantitative analysis techniques.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's cost of quality.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor: not risk parameters.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Other qualitative parameters include urgency, proximity, dormancy, manageability, controllability, detectability, strategic impact.

domande.spiegazione: Assessment of other risk parameters (PMBOK 6, pp. 423-424).

domande.domanda: A large risk could seriously impact the company. Several executives each propose their own response, convinced theirs is best. You decide to settle it with a decision tree. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Rate the risks for probability and impact and get a rating for each.
opzioni.B: Note each option on a vertical bar chart for its sensitivity impact on cost.
opzioni.C: Note the response options with their cost impact and probability of occurrence.
opzioni.D: Run a simulation of all responses against multiple criteria to test their impact.

domande.hint: A decision tree combines costs and probabilities along branches.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's qualitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's a tornado diagram (sensitivity analysis).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Options with their cost/benefit and outcome probabilities, to choose the best path.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Monte Carlo simulation.

domande.spiegazione: Decision tree analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 435).

domande.domanda: You've recently become a PM in a large organization. A colleague tells you the organization has a substantial, directive PMO. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with other PMs in the PMO to find a project that suits your skills.
opzioni.B: Start a business case in your work area to initiate a project.
opzioni.C: Await assignment to a project by the PMO.
opzioni.D: Review the PM frameworks, templates and tools mandated by the PMO.

domande.hint: Supportive, controlling, directive: which one manages projects directly?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In a directive PMO you don't choose your project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You don't have that autonomy here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A directive PMO directly manages projects and assigns project managers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That describes a controlling PMO.

domande.spiegazione: PMO types: supportive (templates), controlling (compliance), directive (manages projects, assigns PMs) (PMBOK 6, p. 48).

domande.domanda: The customer worries the project isn't delivering fast enough. You review schedule and cost: actual cost = $648,000, earned value = $601,000, planned value = $629,000. How is the project performing?

opzioni.A: Ahead of schedule and under budget.
opzioni.B: Ahead of schedule and over budget.
opzioni.C: Behind schedule and over budget.
opzioni.D: Behind schedule and under budget.

domande.hint: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. EV < PV means behind schedule, and EV < AC means over budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. EV < PV means behind schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. SV = 601 - 629 = -28k (behind schedule); CV = 601 - 648 = -47k (over budget).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. EV < AC means over budget.

domande.spiegazione: Earned value analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 261).
domande.nota: The transcript quotes SV -38,000 and CV -28,000: the values here are recomputed from the figures.

domande.domanda: The people and resources are costing a lot and the sponsor comments frequently. You check: PV = $840,000, EV = $795,000, AC = $755,000. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Use the project contingency reserves.
opzioni.B: Raise a change request to reduce scope and bring cost back on track.
opzioni.C: Reduce the project resources to bring cost back on track.
opzioni.D: Add more resources to bring the schedule back on track.

domande.hint: Check the data, not the perception.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're under budget: no need for reserves.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Cost isn't the problem.
