opzioni.A: Create a performance improvement plan.
opzioni.B: Workshop the resource management plan.
opzioni.C: Workshop the team charter with the team.
opzioni.D: Interview each team member.

domande.hint: Agree on ways of working together.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An improvement plan is punitive and not collaborative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. PM's process, not the team's working agreements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Defines values, agreements, roles and operating guidelines.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Individual interviews are slower than a joint workshop.

domande.spiegazione: Team charter (PMBOK 8, pp. 81, 142).

domande.domanda: Michelle's recently formed smart grid team has conflicts, with members doing tasks others think are theirs. The first deliverable date was missed. What next?

opzioni.A: Workshop a responsibility assignment matrix with the team.
opzioni.B: Identify the team as being in the storming stage.
opzioni.C: Update the schedule.
opzioni.D: Workshop the resource breakdown structure.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A RAM (e.g. RACI) clarifies responsibilities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Recognizing the storming stage is a diagnosis, not an action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Moving the date doesn't fix unclear responsibilities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Shows hierarchy, not responsibilities.

domande.spiegazione: RAM (PMBOK 8, pp. 81, 194).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Claire leads a reporting work stream at Iron Peak Consulting. Many small tasks that should take a few hours were given weeks to complete, and the extra time filled up with unforeseen scope, straining the budget. Claire knows she must limit the time available for these tasks, applying:

opzioni.A: Schedule compression.
opzioni.B: Resource leveling.
opzioni.C: Parkinson's law.
opzioni.D: Fast tracking.

domande.hint: Work expands to fill the time available.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Compression shortens the overall schedule; it doesn't explain why small tasks grow.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Leveling resolves over-allocation of the same resource.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Parkinson's law: work expands to fill the time given, so limit the time available.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fast tracking runs sequential activities in parallel.

domande.spiegazione: Organizational theory, Parkinson's law (PMBOK 8, pp. 81, 184).

domande.domanda: Richard is estimating resources for a nationwide telecom rollout at Northwest Communications. Many combinations of crews, equipment and timelines are possible, making it hard to identify the most efficient allocation. Which technique is best?

opzioni.A: Analogous estimating.
opzioni.B: Genetic algorithms.
opzioni.C: Bottom-up estimating.
opzioni.D: Expert judgment sessions.

domande.hint: Too many combinations to evaluate by hand.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Estimates from a similar project; it doesn't optimize combinations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. An AI optimization technique inspired by natural selection: it iteratively explores combinations and keeps the fittest.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Sums work package estimates; it doesn't choose between allocations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Valuable, but people can't explore that many combinations efficiently.

domande.spiegazione: Genetic algorithms (PMBOK 8, pp. 82, 171).

domande.domanda: At North Shore Grid, you're finalizing planning for a substation upgrade. After defining scope and sequencing activities, you determine the types and quantities of resources needed for each work package. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Prepare the resource calendar.
opzioni.B: Update the work breakdown structure.
opzioni.C: Develop the responsibility assignment matrix.
opzioni.D: Create a resource breakdown structure.

domande.hint: What is the output of Estimate Resources?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The resource calendar is an output of Acquire Resources, later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The WBS is already done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Useful, but it assigns responsibilities rather than representing the estimated resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The RBS is a hierarchical representation of resources by category and type, an output of Estimate Resources.

domande.spiegazione: Estimate Resources; RBS (PMBOK 8, pp. 82, 132).

domande.domanda: At CE Group, two department leads argue over releasing key specialists assigned to your project. Each insists their internal deadlines come first, creating uncertainty about when the resources can join. What is the most appropriate action?

opzioni.A: Adjust the schedule baseline to reflect limited resource access.
opzioni.B: Review resource calendars to determine availability and negotiate a realistic allocation.
opzioni.C: Request extra budget to hire external resources and avoid the conflict.
opzioni.D: Revise the stakeholder engagement plan to address the managers' concerns.

domande.hint: Direct and collaborative, based on real availability.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Premature: try to solve the conflict first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Calendars show actual availability, and negotiation reaches a realistic allocation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Avoid adding cost or resources when the problem can be negotiated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possibly later; it doesn't resolve the immediate allocation.

domande.spiegazione: Acquire Resources; resource calendar (PMBOK 8, pp. 82-84, 132).

domande.domanda: Midway through execution, several team members say their concerns are dismissed and obstacles remain unresolved. Some blame others for underperforming as work stalls. What should the PM do?

opzioni.A: Reassign underperforming team members to keep timelines.
opzioni.B: Update the resource management plan with team assessment results.
opzioni.C: Increase reporting frequency to track progress more closely.
opzioni.D: Use active listening and remove the impediments the team raises.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't address dismissed concerns or blockers; not collaborative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A planning document doesn't solve the team's frustration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Adds burden without removing obstacles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Servant leadership supports team needs: listening and removing impediments addresses the root of the frustration.

domande.spiegazione: Lead the Team; servant leadership (PMBOK 8, pp. 84-85, 197).

domande.domanda: Dylan leads software delivery at Quantum Leap Systems. The team completes iterations, but recurring collaboration and workflow issues slow progress and nothing usable has been delivered for some time. What should Dylan do next?

opzioni.A: Perform team assessments.
opzioni.B: Facilitate daily stand-up meetings.
opzioni.C: Conduct a retrospective with the team.
opzioni.D: Invite real system users to sprint planning.

domande.hint: Recurring process problems: inspect and adapt.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Evaluates individuals rather than improving the way of working.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Helps raise daily blockers but doesn't fix recurring workflow issues.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A retrospective reviews work and results to improve process and product; it can be held anytime progress stalls.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Users belong in the sprint review, not planning.

domande.spiegazione: Retrospectives (PMBOK 8, pp. 85, 194).

domande.domanda: Louise leads a global software integration at SG Tech. The team has worked through conflicts, improved skills and is building trust, but members wait for her direction before deciding anything, creating bottlenecks. What will she do next?

opzioni.A: Use autocratic decision making.
opzioni.B: Apply distributed management and leadership with the team.
opzioni.C: Increase stand-ups and reporting frequency.
opzioni.D: Use servant leadership with the team.

domande.hint: A maturing team, slowed by one decision maker.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's essentially the current bottleneck.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Decentralizes decision making and authority across the team, reducing reliance on the PM.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. More admin doesn't remove the bottleneck.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good in general, but distributed management directly addresses centralized decisions.

domande.spiegazione: Distributed management and leadership (PMBOK 8, pp. 85, 168).

domande.domanda: Brian leads a data migration at Zendu Systems with a recently formed team. Members challenge each other's approaches, disagreements slow progress and priorities are frequently debated. Which stage is the team in?

opzioni.A: Forming.
opzioni.B: Storming.
opzioni.C: Norming.
opzioni.D: Performing.

domande.hint: Tuckman: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Forming is the initial, polite phase when members come together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Storming: members address work and approaches with conflict and debate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Norming comes once the team finds its rhythm and working norms.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Performing is a trusting, high-performing team.

domande.spiegazione: Tuckman ladder (PMBOK 8). To move to norming: team charter, RACI, problem solving.
domande.nota: The instructor doesn't cite a specific page.

domande.domanda: At Kendra Labs, the team is spread across different departments in the same building and collaborates by video conference. There have been misunderstandings about requirements, and members are slow to learn the new system. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Co-locate the team.
opzioni.B: Conduct team-building sessions.
opzioni.C: Increase the frequency of meetings.
opzioni.D: Create thorough requirements documentation.

domande.hint: They're already in the same building.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Co-location improves communication, relationships and learning through osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't directly address misunderstandings or learning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. More meetings don't fix the root cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Documentation doesn't replace collaboration.

domande.spiegazione: Co-location (PMBOK 8, pp. 85, 151-152).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads co-location last and answers A.

domande.domanda: Sydney manages a commercial building project at Altura Construction. A key stakeholder became resistant after missing updates: they can't attend key meetings and don't read emailed reports. What will Sydney do?

opzioni.A: Use an interactive communication approach.
opzioni.B: Apply a push communication approach.
opzioni.C: Use a pull communication approach.
opzioni.D: Update the stakeholder engagement plan.

domande.hint: Emails (push) and meetings (interactive) aren't reaching them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Interactive needs them in meetings, which they can't attend.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Emailed reports are already push communication, and they don't work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A portal or repository lets the stakeholder access information whenever they can.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't change how information reaches them.

domande.spiegazione: Monitor and Control Resourcing; communication methods (PMBOK 8, pp. 87, 152).

domande.domanda: Taylor, PM at Summit Build, hears differing views from team leads during a nationwide rollout: some say certain resources underperform with issues and defects, others say performance is fine. It's unclear whether action is needed. What should Taylor do?

opzioni.A: Increase supervision of both teams.
opzioni.B: Perform a root cause analysis.
opzioni.C: Adjust the schedule for upcoming inefficiencies.
opzioni.D: Use control charts to review performance trends.

domande.hint: First confirm with data whether there's a problem.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Premature without evidence.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful once a problem is confirmed: here it isn't yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assumes a problem that may not exist.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Control charts show whether the process is stable and predictable, settling the disagreement with data.

domande.spiegazione: Control charts (PMBOK 8, pp. 87, 158).

domande.domanda: At VL Systems, stakeholders are raising possible future threats, but there's no agreement on how risks will be identified, analyzed or monitored, and planning is slowing because of uncertain decision making. What should Cameron do next?

opzioni.A: Brainstorm risks with the team and add them to the risk register.
opzioni.B: Develop the risk management plan.
opzioni.C: Perform qualitative risk analysis to prioritize the risks.
opzioni.D: Plan risk responses to reduce uncertainty.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Part of the process, but you first need to agree how.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Defines how risk management will be conducted; started early in the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A later step in the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A later step in the process.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Risk Management (PMBOK 8, pp. 95-96, 134).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads the RMP first and answers B.

domande.domanda: At Apex Nova Solutions, a workshop identifies several potential events that could negatively affect the project. Some want to move straight to delivery, others are worried about the impact. What should you do next?

opzioni.A: Document the risk responses for the events.
opzioni.B: Review the threats at the stage gate review.
opzioni.C: Conduct a risk audit.
opzioni.D: Develop the risk register.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Responses come after recording and analyzing the risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The PM manages risks rather than pushing them to governance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Audits check the risk process, not individual risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The risk register captures identified risks so they can be analyzed and monitored.

domande.spiegazione: Identify Risks; risk register (PMBOK 8, pp. 96-97, 137).

domande.domanda: Ryan is planning a logistics optimization project at HLT. He wants to get ahead of impacts over the project's life, but the team is new to the industry and needs a more structured approach. What will Ryan do next?

opzioni.A: Conduct a brainstorming session.
opzioni.B: Develop the risk register.
opzioni.C: Perform a risk audit.
opzioni.D: Perform a SWOT analysis.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Unstructured for an inexperienced team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Records risks but doesn't help identify them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reviews the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. SWOT structures identification around strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats.

domande.spiegazione: SWOT analysis (PMBOK 8, pp. 97, 204).

domande.domanda: During planning at Venture Innovations, the team identifies several risks to cost, schedule and quality. With limited budget, not all can be addressed at once. What should the PM do next?

opzioni.A: Develop the risk register.
opzioni.B: Plan the risk responses.
opzioni.C: Perform qualitative risk analysis.
opzioni.D: Perform sensitivity analysis.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Risks are already identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You need priorities before responding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Prioritizes risks by probability, impact and other characteristics.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Quantitative and more effortful; prioritization comes first.

domande.spiegazione: Perform Risk Analysis (PMBOK 8, pp. 96-98).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads qualitative last and answers C.

domande.domanda: Andre at Blue Peak Telecom identifies a risk that could delay a key deliverable. The team disagrees on handling it. The risk can't be fully removed, but its likelihood or impact can be reduced. What should Andre do?

opzioni.A: Mitigate the risk.
opzioni.B: Transfer the risk.
opzioni.C: Accept the risk.
opzioni.D: Implement a contingency reserve.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Mitigation reduces the probability and/or impact of a threat.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Transfer shifts ownership (insurance, contracts).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Acceptance takes no proactive action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A reserve funds the response but doesn't reduce the risk.

domande.spiegazione: Strategies for threats: avoid, escalate, transfer, mitigate, accept (PMBOK 8, pp. 96-99, 203).

domande.domanda: At Silverline Infrastructure, Lorna is executing a highway expansion. A planned response to a major risk requires extra work and impacts both timeline and budget. The team is ready to proceed. What should Lorna do next?

opzioni.A: Adjust the project schedule and budget.
opzioni.B: Implement the planned response.
opzioni.C: Submit a change request.
opzioni.D: Communicate the risk to stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only after the change is approved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Only after approval, since baselines change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Impacts on baselines go through change control first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Done after the decision.

domande.spiegazione: Implement Risk Responses; change requests (PMBOK 8, pp. 98, 100, 116).

domande.domanda: Rachel monitors risks on a warehouse automation project. Several identified risks occurred and cost a lot. The sponsor asks if the project is on track and whether there's enough to cover the remaining risk responses. What should Rachel do?

opzioni.A: Review the risk register for remaining risks.
opzioni.B: Perform reserve analysis.
opzioni.C: Conduct a risk audit.
opzioni.D: Conduct a project risk assessment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Lists risks but doesn't assess reserve sufficiency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Evaluates remaining risk against schedule and budget reserves.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reviews the risk process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Identifies and assesses risks, not reserves.

domande.spiegazione: Monitor Risks; reserve analysis (PMBOK 8, pp. 98, 100, 192).

domande.domanda: Evelyn has just taken over a digital transformation at SBG. There are concerns that the initiative won't deliver the expected business value after rollout. She needs to know who is getting value from the project. What will she do next?

opzioni.A: Review the business case.
opzioni.B: Review the stakeholder classification.
opzioni.C: Perform a cost-benefit analysis.
opzioni.D: Review the benefits management plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Justifies the investment, but doesn't detail benefit ownership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Shows influence and impact, not benefits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A prioritization tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Describes how benefits are created, maximized, sustained and who receives them.

domande.spiegazione: Benefits management plan (PMBOK 8, p. 115).

domande.domanda: Paige manages a medical device project at Synapse Biotech. Different teams use different versions of design documents, causing inconsistencies and rework; changes aren't tracked. She wants control over versions and updates. Which approach?

opzioni.A: Use a configuration management plan.
opzioni.B: Use a change management plan.
opzioni.C: Use the scope management plan.
opzioni.D: Create and update the change log.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Defines procedures to track artifacts and control versions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Defines the change process, not version control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Covers scope only.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only one step within the process.

domande.spiegazione: Configuration management plan (PMBOK 8, p. 118).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor's 'answer I' is interpreted as A.

domande.domanda: Chloe facilitates a requirements workshop at NR Group. It produces a large set of ideas from many stakeholders, making patterns hard to identify. What will she do next?

opzioni.A: Conduct interviews.
opzioni.B: Use the nominal group technique.
opzioni.C: Use brainstorming.
opzioni.D: Use an affinity diagram.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Slower and generates more input, not structure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful for anonymous prioritization, not grouping.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Generates even more ideas.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Classifies large numbers of ideas into groups by similarity.

domande.spiegazione: Affinity diagram (PMBOK 8, p. 145).

domande.domanda: Nathan has joined a large aerospace project at WS Dynamics as a new PM. He doesn't know the internal departments and reporting lines, and key stakeholders are being missed. What should he do next?

opzioni.A: Create a stakeholder register.
opzioni.B: Develop the communications management plan.
opzioni.C: Review the organizational breakdown structure.
opzioni.D: Conduct stakeholder interviews.

domande.hint: First learn how the organization is structured.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You need to know who they are first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too early: stakeholders aren't identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The OBS shows organizational units and their relationship to project activities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You don't yet know whom to interview.

domande.spiegazione: Organizational breakdown structure (PMBOK 8, p. 171).

domande.domanda: Megan is scheduling a store renovation at Sideline Interiors. Flooring installation must wait until painting is fully completed, but furniture assembly can begin once painting has started. Which sequence reflects this?

opzioni.A: Painting→Flooring finish-to-start; Painting→Furniture start-to-start.
opzioni.B: Painting→Flooring start-to-start; Painting→Furniture finish-to-start.
opzioni.C: Painting→Flooring finish-to-finish; Painting→Furniture start-to-start.
opzioni.D: Painting→Flooring finish-to-start; Painting→Furniture finish-to-finish.

domande.hint: 'Wait until finished' = FS; 'can begin once started' = SS.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Flooring starts when painting finishes (FS); furniture starts once painting starts (SS).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The relationships are swapped.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Flooring is finish-to-start, not finish-to-finish.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Furniture is start-to-start, not finish-to-finish.

domande.spiegazione: Precedence diagramming method (PMBOK 8, p. 185).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed: the instructor confirms FS + SS as answer A.

domande.domanda: Adrian evaluates vendor proposals. Stakeholders disagree on the supplier, citing cost, experience and technical capability, and proposals are so different they're hard to compare. What will he do next?

opzioni.A: Perform a make-or-buy analysis.
opzioni.B: Conduct a bidder conference.
opzioni.C: Define the source selection criteria.
opzioni.D: Develop a procurement management plan.

domande.hint: A common basis to compare proposals.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The buy decision has already been made.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Shares information with sellers, not evaluation priorities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Criteria (capability, cost, delivery, expertise, experience) align stakeholders and make proposals comparable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Broader process; less direct.

domande.spiegazione: Source selection criteria (PMBOK 8, Appendix, pp. 249-250).

domande.domanda: Sophie manages a highway project at Delta Core. A contractor claims extra costs due to unexpected site conditions. Both parties want to resolve it quickly without external parties or delays. What should she do?

opzioni.A: Engage a mediator.
opzioni.B: Initiate negotiation with the contractor.
opzioni.C: Refer the claim to arbitration.
opzioni.D: Document the claim and update the issue log.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A third party: they want to avoid that.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Direct negotiation is the first step and avoids third parties.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A later step with a third party.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful record-keeping, but doesn't resolve the claim.

domande.spiegazione: Claims administration: negotiation, mediation, arbitration, dispute boards, litigation (PMBOK 8, pp. 252-253).

domande.domanda: Carlos manages an e-commerce upgrade at VR Systems. Stakeholders keep requesting small feature additions that the team implements without formal review. Timelines slip and costs rise. What is causing this situation?

opzioni.A: Scope validation is performed without stakeholder approval.
opzioni.B: The change control process is being bypassed.
opzioni.C: Gold plating.
opzioni.D: Scope creep.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Validation is about accepting deliverables, not this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's how it happens, but the phenomenon described is scope creep.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Gold plating is the team adding features no one asked for: here stakeholders request them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Uncontrolled expansion of scope without adjusting time, cost or resources.

domande.spiegazione: Scope creep (PMBOK 8, p. 273).

domande.domanda: Matthew reviews system upgrade proposals with different investments and returns. The sponsor wants to prioritize by ROI: A 45%, B 90%, C 135%, D 110%. Which should be chosen?

opzioni.A: Proposal A (45%).
opzioni.B: Proposal B (90%).
opzioni.C: Proposal C (135%).
opzioni.D: Proposal D (110%).

domande.hint: For ROI, NPV, IRR and BCR higher is better; only payback is better when shorter.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. 45% is the lowest return.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Lower than C and D.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. 135% is the highest ROI.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but lower than C.

domande.spiegazione: ROI = net gain / investment x 100 (PMBOK 8).

file.titolo: 150 PMBOK 7 Scenario-Based PMP Exam Questions and Answers

domande.domanda: You've been assigned to a project that is behind schedule. The team is relatively new, conflicts are arising, members blame each other for work not done and some don't show up at all. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Meet the functional manager to agree on team members' time commitments.
opzioni.B: Meet the team to set a team charter and define roles and responsibilities.
opzioni.C: Ask the sponsor for funding for resources who can work together.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the steering committee as a project risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Time commitments don't address the conflict or blame.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A team charter and clear roles create a collaborative team environment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. New people won't guarantee no conflict: managing it is the PM's job.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening (an issue) and should be managed before escalating.

domande.spiegazione: Create a collaborative team environment: team agreements, roles and responsibilities (PMBOK 7, pp. 28-29).

domande.domanda: You completed a project for a new product and are asked to keep the product relevant in the marketplace after release. Half the team is rolling off and the project budget is nearly depleted. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a business case and project charter for the sponsor.
opzioni.B: Retain as many current project staff as possible.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request to keep adding scope to the current project.
opzioni.D: Secure funding for a stable team and use research to form a suite of projects improving the product.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fits one specific project, not ongoing product management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. There's no money left to pay them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project is ending: adding scope isn't the way.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Product management uses a stable team, funded over the product life cycle.

domande.spiegazione: Product management considerations (PMBOK 7, pp. 17-19).

domande.domanda: Delivering a critical change, several key stakeholders add seemingly unnecessary approvals, reports and meetings and restrict the people you need from working on your project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Go directly to the people you need to avoid back and forth with the stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk about insufficient resource access.
opzioni.C: Communicate more often with the stakeholders and gain deeper awareness of their ideas and situation.
opzioni.D: Show the stakeholders the resource assignment matrix and roles.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Going behind their backs damages the relationship.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Logging a risk doesn't manage it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Stakeholders add steps or restrict people when not engaged: communication and awareness help.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. May win minds but not hearts: they still aren't engaged.

domande.spiegazione: Effectively engage with stakeholders (PMBOK 7, pp. 32-33).

domande.domanda: Your team is mostly men. Jane was recently hired for her high expertise, but she is left out of key meetings, her opinions are overlooked, and she is paid significantly less than her male colleagues. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take steps to bring her pay in line with others and ask for her opinion in every meeting along with the rest of the team.
opzioni.B: Take the lower pay as a win to keep costs down; colleagues don't need to know.
opzioni.C: Ask Jane to write down her industry knowledge in case she leaves.
opzioni.D: Don't rock the boat: this is how the industry works.

domande.hint: Stewardship: fairness in pay, opportunity and treatment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Respectful engagement includes fair compensation, access to opportunity and treatment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Unfair and destroys engagement when discovered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Capturing knowledge is fine but doesn't fix the unfairness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Accepting the status quo isn't stewardship.

domande.spiegazione: Be a diligent, respectful and caring steward (PMBOK 7, p. 25).

domande.domanda: In a working group, a stakeholder says the product you're working on will be discontinued in the next 5 months. Your budget is approved until scheduled delivery, also in 5 months. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Keep the project going: the discontinued product isn't your responsibility.
opzioni.B: Meet the sponsor to share the information and recommend terminating the project.
opzioni.C: Change the project scope to a different product so it stays relevant.
opzioni.D: Ask for extra funding to improve the product instead of discontinuing it.

domande.hint: Value is the primary motivator for a project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Stewardship means acting on this information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. If the project no longer aligns with the business need, the organization may terminate it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A project is initiated for a specific purpose; changing it entirely needs a new project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Speculative and may not reverse the decision.

domande.spiegazione: Focus on value (PMBOK 7, p. 35).

domande.domanda: While creating the scope statement and WBS, you notice some database functionality that would help a different project in your PMO. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Place the feature in the other project's backlog and ask them to prioritize it.
opzioni.B: Raise it as a threat in the risk register with a mitigate response.
opzioni.C: Add the scope to your project and complete it as soon as possible.
opzioni.D: Raise it as an opportunity with an exploit response and meet the other project's team and sponsor.

domande.hint: Systems thinking: it's a positive risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't add to another team's backlog without talking to them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an opportunity, not a threat.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Your team isn't the expert in that product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Make the opportunity known and exploit it, collaborating with the other project.

domande.spiegazione: Respond to system interactions (PMBOK 7, pp. 39, 129).

domande.domanda: On a high-profile project, several senior executives want credit while limiting impact to their own resources, causing conflicts and an unclear scope statement that risks failure. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the scope statement yourself to avoid more conflict.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a discussion with the executives as a neutral third party, focusing on agreed goals.
opzioni.C: Limit project resources to the executives until they agree.
opzioni.D: Escalate to the steering committee to resolve.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Without their agreement it may never be accepted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Neutral facilitation helps more than recommendations when senior managers conflict.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wastes funded resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Manage it first before escalating.

domande.spiegazione: Demonstrate leadership behaviors (PMBOK 7, p. 42).

domande.domanda: Most of the product is planned upfront, but an external system will come from a vendor in partial pieces with unclear requirements. Half the stakeholders want waterfall, half want agile. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use agile: the fixed scope is low risk and changes are captured.
opzioni.B: Use waterfall and ask the team to plan the uncertain scope better.
opzioni.C: Proceed with a hybrid method: pre-planned scope with agile ceremonies that promote feedback.
opzioni.D: Combine waterfall and agile to capture all requirements and keep stakeholders happy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Ignores the upfront-planned part.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Uncertain scope can't simply be planned better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Hybrid uses predictive and adaptive only where each fits; tailoring is iterative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Similar, but 'hybrid' tailored to context is the precise answer.

domande.spiegazione: Tailoring (PMBOK 7, pp. 44-46).

domande.domanda: Senior users testing released parts found missing requirements and defects. Their manager fears the product won't be fit for purpose on time. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Do some testing yourself to ensure quality.
opzioni.B: Help every team member focus on quality, from correct acceptance criteria to a developed and tested product.
opzioni.C: Limit testing until the end so it's done in one go.
opzioni.D: Increase testing and add more testers so no defect goes unnoticed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The PM is the conductor, not the tester.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Builds quality into processes and deliverables across the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile tests at all levels throughout.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Throws resources at it without building quality in.

domande.spiegazione: Build quality into processes and deliverables (PMBOK 7, pp. 47-49).

domande.domanda: Your team struggles to come up with risks. You decide to guide them on the types of complexity that might affect the new product. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask them to brainstorm qualitative and quantitative risks.
opzioni.B: Ask them to perform 5 Whys and Ishikawa analysis.
opzioni.C: Ask them to brainstorm around unwanted human behavior, system behavior, ambiguity and technical innovation impacts.
opzioni.D: Ask them to hold a retrospective.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't guide them on complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Root cause tools for an existing problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Complexity comes from human behavior, system interactions, uncertainty, ambiguity and innovation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reviews past work, not future risks.

domande.spiegazione: Navigate complexity (PMBOK 7, pp. 50-51).

domande.domanda: You discover a negative risk with a potential impact of $2,000,000. Stakeholders decide it is within their risk appetite, provided a risk threshold of 10% is met. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $200,000.
opzioni.B: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $1.8M to $2.2M.
opzioni.C: Note the impact as outside the acceptable risk level of $2,000,000.
opzioni.D: Note the impact as an opportunity of $200,000.

domande.hint: The threshold is a variation around the objective.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. $200,000 is the size of the variation, not the acceptable range.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A 10% threshold around $2M gives an acceptable range of $1.8M to $2.2M.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders said it is within their appetite.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's a threat, not an opportunity.

domande.spiegazione: Risk appetite = uncertainty stakeholders accept; risk threshold = acceptable variation around an objective (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 11.

domande.domanda: A risk has been raised about insufficient building materials. A response assigned to the functional manager suggests using a brand-new, not fully tested material. Half of the stakeholders support it; the other half refuse to sign off. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Suggest a quantitative risk approach to give a more accurate financial impact.
opzioni.B: Suggest they proceed with the proposed response and ensure it is followed through.
opzioni.C: Suggest a different risk owner, as an executive may have more power to respond.
opzioni.D: Suggest a different risk response, as responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic and agreed by relevant stakeholders.

domande.hint: What characteristics should a good risk response have?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More analysis isn't needed yet; the response itself is the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't force it while half the stakeholders disagree.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. An executive could force it through, but the disagreement may have good reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A response must be appropriate, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by stakeholders and owned.

domande.spiegazione: Risk responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by relevant stakeholders and owned by a responsible person (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 12.

domande.domanda: Your project went off track due to uncertainty in requirements and resources. You reined it in at significant cost, and the PMO asks you to brainstorm with the team how to prevent it happening again. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to increase the contingency reserve to allow for these impacts.
opzioni.B: Ask the team to change the methodology from waterfall to agile.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to use short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning.
opzioni.D: Ask the team to check their work twice before sending it on.

domande.hint: How does a team embrace adaptability and resiliency?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More money doesn't improve the way of working.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changing methodology doesn't magically remove uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning build adaptability and resiliency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible, but much weaker than C.

domande.spiegazione: Embrace adaptability and resiliency: short feedback loops, continuous learning, inspection and adaptation, transparent planning, prototypes (PMBOK 7, p. 56).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 13.

domande.domanda: As your project progresses, many business stakeholders voice concerns, question the changes and even miss key meetings, trying to sabotage your efforts. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Communicate the vision and benefits of the change clearly, along with the impact on their work.
opzioni.B: Create an impact/influence chart to determine who should be engaged.
opzioni.C: Escalate to the sponsor and arrange for different stakeholders.
opzioni.D: Map the current state and proposed future state of the change for the stakeholders.

domande.hint: Resistance to change usually comes from a lack of understanding.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Communicating vision, benefits and impact early reduces resistance and change fatigue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful, but it doesn't address people questioning the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders usually can't be replaced: work with them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close (it's problem solving), but communication is the key to engagement here.

domande.spiegazione: Change management: communicate vision, goals and benefits early, with the impact on work processes (PMBOK 7, p. 59).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 14.

domande.domanda: Analyzing stakeholders with an impact/influence chart, you find more than 100 groups and over 3,000 impacted stakeholders. Other parts of the project are falling behind as you try to keep up. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the project team to engage different groups so everyone is covered.
opzioni.B: Clearly prioritize the stakeholders, then engage and communicate with the highly impacted and influential groups early and often.
opzioni.C: Monitor stakeholders for signs of stress and respond to the most stressed groups.
opzioni.D: Create a SharePoint page that any stakeholder can consult at any time.

domande.hint: Too many stakeholders to engage effectively: what's the key word?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Splitting the work makes sense, but isn't the specific technique.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. When there are too many to engage effectively, prioritization is key.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's a kind of prioritization, but less complete than B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good pull communication, but doesn't solve the overload.

domande.spiegazione: Stakeholder engagement: identify, understand and analyze, prioritize, engage, monitor (PMBOK 7, pp. 11-12).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 15.

domande.domanda: Your project has mostly used pull communication with the customer. Monitoring engagement, you notice stakeholders are unclear on the impacts or benefits. You decide to add push communication. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a SharePoint web page with all the project information.
opzioni.B: Push for more funding and communicate this to the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Push stakeholders to engage in more two-way communication.
opzioni.D: Send a weekly email to stakeholders with a project update, including impacts and benefits.

domande.hint: Push = sent to recipients; pull = they fetch it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A web page is pull communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Right keyword, wrong meaning: funding isn't the issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Right keyword, but it isn't push communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A sent email is push communication.

domande.spiegazione: Push: memos, emails, status reports, voicemail. Pull: bulletins, web pages, whiteboards (PMBOK 7, p. 13).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 16.

domande.domanda: You have taken over a project with a vendor where scope and requirements have been missed, and miscommunication is common. You set an extremely important meeting with your team and the vendor's team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Speak slowly and clearly to the vendor's team, at a louder volume if necessary.
opzioni.B: Confirm they heard your message, determine whether they agree and identify any nuanced or unintended messages.
opzioni.C: Only communicate with the vendor in writing to have a trail of proof.
opzioni.D: Prepare a claim for the mishandled scope through the procurement team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Volume doesn't improve understanding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quick feedback loops confirm the message was heard, agreed and correctly interpreted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Writing loses tone and body language and is more easily misread.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fix the communication first.

domande.spiegazione: Feedback loops: confirm the message was heard, check agreement, identify nuances (PMBOK 7, p. 13).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 17.

domande.domanda: Stakeholders seem engaged, but frequent changes to scope and requirements are causing delays, with issues raised and multiple feedback rounds. You're not sure who or what is causing it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform root cause analysis with the team to brainstorm the problem.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk for the project delay and review responses with the team.
opzioni.C: Review the issue log, risk register and change log for the most frequent requesters, then update your engagement approach for them.
opzioni.D: Ensure the budget has enough contingency reserve for the reviews and delays.

domande.hint: Frequent changes may signal stakeholders who are not aligned. How do you find out who?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but C goes further: it finds the who and acts on it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an issue already happening, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The logs reveal which stakeholders drive the changes, so you can engage them better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't just throw money at it.

domande.spiegazione: Many changes may mean stakeholders aren't engaged/aligned; issue and risk registers reveal challenges with individual stakeholders (PMBOK 7, p. 15).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 18.

domande.domanda: A manager leads in a dictatorship style; the team has stopped making suggestions, sick days have increased and work has slowed. You suggest servant leadership. What will they do next?

opzioni.A: Serve the team as much as possible, ensuring their every need is met.
opzioni.B: Focus on obstacle removal, encouragement and development opportunities.
opzioni.C: Ensure team members serve one another and help each other succeed.
opzioni.D: Serve the team new ways of doing the work and engage them through variety.

domande.hint: Servant leadership = removing blockers and growing people.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds good, but servant leaders don't meet every need.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Obstacle removal, diversion shielding, encouragement and development are servant leadership behaviors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but not servant leadership specifically.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Right keywords, wrong meaning.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leaders enable self-organization and autonomy, remove obstacles, shield the team and offer development (PMBOK 7, p. 18).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 19.

domande.domanda: You have been allocated to a new team with members from different functional areas, few of whom have worked on a project before. Miscommunication and rework are causing delays. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set a daily stand-up so they update what they completed.
opzioni.B: Review the resource assignment matrix to ensure they are doing their job.
opzioni.C: Help the team set its vision and objectives, roles and responsibilities, and team operations.
opzioni.D: Send team members on training in their roles.

domande.hint: A newly formed team needs clarity first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Could help, but doesn't create shared clarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Could help, but is control rather than team development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Vision, roles and ways of working (e.g. a team charter) build a one-team mindset.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the issue is alignment, not individual skill.

domande.spiegazione: Teams formed across organizations need upfront work: shared vision, clear roles, ways of working (PMBOK 7, p. 18).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 20.

domande.domanda: You've collected requirements, matched them to scope and broken them into activities. You notice the marketing manager added extra scope unrelated to your project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise the incorrect scope items and their impact and start an open dialogue with the manager.
opzioni.B: Override the marketing manager's decision as the senior PM.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request and let the CCB decide.
opzioni.D: Place the extra scope in the product backlog for the product owner to prioritize.

domande.hint: Maybe it was a mistake or previously approved.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Open dialogue and courage are key to a positive team culture.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Forcing the decision damages the relationship.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. First understand whether a change is even needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Talk it through first: it may belong to another project.

domande.spiegazione: Project team culture (PMBOK 7, p. 21).

domande.domanda: Your team is protected by a union agreement. They don't know how to use the product, respond slowly and complain about the work. The sponsor threatens to shut the project down. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set up a new project with different team members and transfer the work.
opzioni.B: Set a clear purpose and vision and pair the team with a customer to show the difference they make.
opzioni.C: Tell the team they will lose their jobs.
opzioni.D: Create a Gantt chart, schedule and burndown so the work is transparent.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not feasible and may produce the same result.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Vision and seeing their impact increase intrinsic motivation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Threats entrench the behavior.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Transparency doesn't fix low engagement.

domande.spiegazione: Leadership skills: vision and motivation (PMBOK 7, pp. 24-25).

domande.domanda: In a scope meeting, the business manager accuses the technology manager of not delivering on past projects; the technology manager accuses the business manager of changing requirements. Both close off further discussion. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Side with the technology manager: scope must be controlled.
opzioni.B: Side with the business manager: always deliver to customer specifications.
opzioni.C: Facilitate respectful communication, focus on the issue in the present and search for alternatives together.
opzioni.D: Make both agree to the change control process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Both views have some truth.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Both views have some truth.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Handled well, conflict leads to better decisions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful later, after resolving the present conflict.

domande.spiegazione: Conflict management (PMBOK 7, p. 29).

domande.domanda: Your team is distributed around the country, including home workers. Some members haven't been able to contribute and the program fears delays. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the program to co-locate all team members.
opzioni.B: Run daily stand-ups and working groups only with members in your area.
opzioni.C: Set team leaders in each area to report back to you.
opzioni.D: Use audio/video for meetings, messaging for ongoing contact and an open team website for all project information.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Rarely feasible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Excludes the others.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Keeps silos.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Technology and transparency keep a distributed team connected.

domande.spiegazione: Distributed project teams (PMBOK 7, p. 30).

domande.domanda: You're initiating a project that will significantly change a sales team's process, while the sale outcome remains the same. The functional manager fears disruption. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Kick off with multiple small deliveries to reduce change impact.
opzioni.B: Kick off with a single delivery at the end, when the process change is complete.
opzioni.C: Kick off with continuous delivery for speed.
opzioni.D: Kick off with periodic deliveries of value as it's ready.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A single process is changed as a whole.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Process re-engineering may deliver only near the end when the new process rolls out.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't fit a single process change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't fit a single process change.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery cadence (PMBOK 7, p. 34).
domande.nota: The instructor finds A and B close.

domande.domanda: Requirements are clear but solution ideas are uncertain. The product owner and experts can't tell which ideas will work. The organization can't afford to get it wrong: past mistakes made customers leave. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an incremental approach.
opzioni.B: Use an iterative approach.
opzioni.C: Use a predictive approach.
opzioni.D: Use a hybrid approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Releasing increments risks scaring customers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Iterative captures changing ideas while delivering in one release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't refine uncertain solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No mix of approaches needed.

domande.spiegazione: Development approaches (PMBOK 7, p. 37; Agile Practice Guide, p. 18).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Requirements are complex and likely to change, and the organization needs usable parts released as fast as possible to capture market share. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an iterative approach.
opzioni.B: Use a predictive approach.
opzioni.C: Use an adaptive approach.
opzioni.D: Use a hybrid approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Releases only once.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Plans upfront, single delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adaptive (agile) combines iterative and incremental, refining with feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No predictive part needed.

domande.spiegazione: Adaptive approach (PMBOK 7, p. 35).

domande.domanda: After a government inquiry, a project must change multiple processes under significant regulatory oversight within 10 months before penalties. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an agile approach to deliver change quickly.
opzioni.B: Use a hybrid approach to respond to change while planning upfront.
opzioni.C: Use a predictive approach.
opzioni.D: Use an iterative approach to improve with feedback.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Documentation and demonstration needs favor predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but regulation points to predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Significant regulatory oversight may require predictive for process documentation and demonstration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible, but regulation points to predictive.

domande.spiegazione: Considerations for selecting a development approach (PMBOK 7, p. 40).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your organization is moving to agile, but your team opposes it: executives previously used velocity to force them to work faster instead of a sustainable pace. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add resources to deliver faster and keep executives away.
opzioni.B: Proceed predictively and deal with consequences later.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to use velocity and iterations despite hesitations.
opzioni.D: Suggest flow-based scheduling with a Kanban board.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't address their concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The organization is moving to agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Forcing lowers engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Flow-based scheduling doesn't use sprints or velocity; it optimizes delivery on capacity.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based scheduling (PMBOK 7, p. 45).

domande.domanda: Your team has never worked on projects and doesn't know waterfall or agile. Requirements may be certain or uncertain with varying risk. What will you do as you begin?

opzioni.A: Use waterfall and plan everything upfront for stability.
opzioni.B: Use general phase definitions: feasibility, design, build, test, deploy, close.
opzioni.C: Use agile to respond to change while capability grows.
opzioni.D: Don't use any approach as long as work gets done.

domande.hint: Phases common to every life cycle.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Assumes certainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. All projects go through these phases: once in waterfall, repeatedly in agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assumes uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A process works better.

domande.spiegazione: Life cycle and phase definitions (PMBOK 7, p. 42).

domande.domanda: In a directive PMO, you must prepare for an upcoming accounting project. You have no team, scope, requirements or timeline yet. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the functional manager for a wish list to take to the PMO.
opzioni.B: Create a project management plan.
opzioni.C: Create a small backlog and start the first sprint.
opzioni.D: Progressively elaborate a vision statement and project charter to define a coordinated approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not a basis to start a project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project doesn't exist yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No direction yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Before initiating, start with a vision statement, charter or business case.

domande.spiegazione: Planning overview (PMBOK 7, p. 52).

domande.domanda: Part of your project delivers a high-value, high-risk component; another part a routine change. The sponsor wants value quickly; the team wants to start with familiar work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Prioritize high-risk items at the end.
opzioni.B: Prioritize high-risk items at the start.
opzioni.C: Use an incremental approach mixing routine and risky work each sprint.
opzioni.D: Plan everything in detail with a baseline and formal change control.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Risk grows if left late.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Novel or risky work early reduces uncertainty before large investment; routine work can wait.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't reduce risk early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't address uncertainty.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery: last responsible moment (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: On an agile project, the functional manager has only high-level requirements and suggests a WBS; the team feels it's for predictive. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the WBS anyway: it's just a tool.
opzioni.B: Use rolling wave planning.
opzioni.C: Note high-level themes or epics, decompose them into features and then user stories.
opzioni.D: Ask for detailed requirements before starting.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but not agile-centric.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but less specific.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Epics → features → stories is decomposition fitting an incremental approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Collaborate to elaborate requirements.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery, decomposition (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: At the beginning of planning, you've broken requirements into deliverables and activities you believe could take 26 weeks. The sponsor asks for an estimate. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Tell the sponsor 26 weeks.
opzioni.B: Say you'll deliver value iteratively until the project stops.
opzioni.C: Tell the sponsor approximately 24-28 weeks.
opzioni.D: Tell the sponsor approximately 20-45 weeks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too precise for so little information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. An estimate is still needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Range too narrow at this stage.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Early estimates have a broad range (about -25% to +75%) that narrows as knowledge grows.

domande.spiegazione: Estimating, range (PMBOK 7, p. 55).

domande.domanda: After analysis, your team estimates a range of 53 to 75 days across all tasks. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note it as high accuracy and low precision.
opzioni.B: Note it as low accuracy and high precision, and ensure estimates become more accurate as the project unfolds.
opzioni.C: Note it as high confidence and low precision.
opzioni.D: Note it as low confidence and high precision.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A wide range is low accuracy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Wide range = low accuracy; days = precise units.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Mixes concepts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Mixes concepts.

domande.spiegazione: Estimating: accuracy, precision, confidence (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your industry is changing significantly and many impacts could affect your benefits. The sponsor asks for the best estimate of benefits. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team for a probabilistic estimate.
opzioni.B: Ask for a deterministic estimate.
opzioni.C: Ask for an absolute estimate.
opzioni.D: Ask for a relative estimate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Ranges with probabilities (e.g. confidence levels) suit uncertain numbers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A single specific number.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A specific actual number.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Compares items; for user stories.

domande.spiegazione: Presenting estimates (PMBOK 7, p. 57).

domande.domanda: The team broke 9 epics into user stories. They size the smallest story as 1 and size others in comparison. Which approach?

opzioni.A: Relative estimating.
opzioni.B: Deterministic estimating.
opzioni.C: Absolute estimating.
opzioni.D: Probabilistic estimating.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Sizing in comparison to other estimates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A single point value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Actual units.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Ranges with probabilities.

domande.spiegazione: Relative estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 57).

domande.domanda: A competitor is building a similar feature; first to market matters. The product owner wants to measure how quickly story cards are completed once development starts. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Measure lead time.
opzioni.B: Check the Gantt chart.
opzioni.C: Measure cycle time.
opzioni.D: Check the schedule network and precedence diagram.

domande.hint: From start of work to done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Lead time runs from request to delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Cycle time is the elapsed time for one unit through the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. For critical path and dependencies.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 58).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your team works flow-based with a Kanban board, not Scrum. You want to estimate how much work can be completed in the next three months. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Multiply velocity by remaining stories.
opzioni.B: Use cycle time and throughput.
opzioni.C: Multiply lead time by SPI.
opzioni.D: Multiply planned value by actual value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Velocity is Scrum.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Flow-based estimates come from cycle time and throughput.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. EVM, not flow.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 58).

domande.domanda: The product owner wants the next feature worked on in parallel with the current one but still released in the existing order. You adjust the backlog and the Gantt roadmap. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Use a schedule lead and change the features to finish-to-start.
opzioni.B: Use a schedule lag and change to finish-to-finish.
opzioni.C: Use a schedule lead and change the features to finish-to-finish.
opzioni.D: Use a schedule lag and change to start-to-start.

domande.hint: Bring forward but keep finish order.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. FS doesn't allow parallel work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A lag delays, not brings forward.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Lead brings it forward; FF keeps the delivery order.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A lag delays.

domande.spiegazione: Schedule lead and lag (PMBOK 7, p. 59; PDM PMBOK 6, p. 190).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Deliverables are done in sequence and work is falling behind. The sponsor wants it sped up but there's no more money. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Apply schedule crashing.
opzioni.B: Apply fast tracking.
opzioni.C: Apply leads and lags.
opzioni.D: Apply resource leveling.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Crashing adds cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Fast tracking performs sequential activities in parallel.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too unspecific.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Leveling may lengthen the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: Fast tracking and crashing (PMBOK 7, p. 59).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You're three weeks behind and can't afford to crash. You check with area leads which deliverables can be fast tracked. Which dependency type is easiest to modify?

opzioni.A: Discretionary dependencies.
opzioni.B: Industry-regulated dependencies.
opzioni.C: External dependencies.
opzioni.D: Mandatory dependencies.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Based on project preferences: might be modifiable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Regulatory needs can't be changed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Usually can't be modified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Usually can't be modified.

domande.spiegazione: Dependencies and compression (PMBOK 7, p. 60).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: discretionary is read last but the transcript gives 'A'.

domande.domanda: Your team, new to agile after waterfall, is asked for a project schedule by a key customer. The team thinks schedules are from the old way. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a Gantt chart of the activities.
opzioni.B: Determine planned versus actual value.
opzioni.C: Tell the customer agile doesn't plan ahead.
opzioni.D: Ask the team to develop a high-level release plan (roadmap) with features per release.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but less agile-centric.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Variance, not a schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile still plans.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Adaptive planning uses a high-level release plan with features per release.

domande.spiegazione: Adaptive schedule planning (PMBOK 7, p. 61).

domande.domanda: Recently agile, your BAs want to gather all requirements and build a full WBS. The product owner says it's too slow. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the scope management plan for the process.
opzioni.B: Break the deliverable into smaller pieces to deliver faster.
opzioni.C: Timebox work on the highest-priority backlog items, update estimates and reprioritize as needed.
opzioni.D: Use the charter's high-level scope to start delivery.

domande.hint: Time boxes on a prioritized backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not adaptive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Pieces must be usable and prioritized.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adaptive approaches use time boxes and a prioritized backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Still needs proper planning.

domande.spiegazione: Time boxes (PMBOK 7, p. 62).
domande.nota: The instructor finds B and C close.

domande.domanda: Reviewing progress, the sponsor notices the solution misses a critical in-scope piece affecting benefits and approves the scope. PV is 520,000 and AC is 535,000. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Work with the PMO to unlock management reserves for the extra work.
opzioni.B: Ask the product owner to reprioritize the backlog.
opzioni.C: Do the work within the normal budget since the project is on track.
opzioni.D: Raise a change request for CCB approval.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Management reserves cover unexpected in-scope work, often managed by the PMO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Bumps other work; not clearly agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You're over budget (AC > PV).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor already approved it.

domande.spiegazione: Budget, management reserve (PMBOK 7, p. 62).

domande.domanda: In planning an agile project with high-level requirements, you must put together a team that can deliver quickly. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Select members from each city for diverse knowledge.
opzioni.B: Create a resource management plan.
opzioni.C: Ask the PMO for available resources.
opzioni.D: Select a small team that can work in the same area to solve problems as they arise.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Distribution slows collaboration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. No strategy yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Availability isn't the criterion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Small co-located teams benefit from osmotic communication.

domande.spiegazione: Project team composition (PMBOK 7, p. 64).

domande.domanda: You're building a team to roll out an accounting system nobody in the organization has used. The project is high risk and must be right first time. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Select a small co-located team.
opzioni.B: Use a predictive approach and source part of the team externally.
opzioni.C: Train internal staff on the system first.
opzioni.D: Perform a make-or-buy analysis.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Nobody internally knows the system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Outside skills weighed against cost; single high-risk delivery suits predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Slow and adds team-forming issues.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Already decided.

domande.spiegazione: Project team composition (PMBOK 7, p. 63).

domande.domanda: You're planning communications for a change affecting nearly 10,000 stakeholders, already identified and prioritized. What would you NOT include in your communication plan?

opzioni.A: Why information should be shared with stakeholders.
opzioni.B: The best way to provide information.
opzioni.C: How stakeholders can make changes to the communication plan.
opzioni.D: When and how often information is needed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. (NOT) Stakeholders give feedback; the team maintains the plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.

domande.spiegazione: Communication planning: who, why, when, how, what (PMBOK 7, p. 64).

domande.domanda: You ordered a large amount of physical inventory from overseas during execution; global supply chains were disrupted and delivery was delayed 3 months. What should you have done differently?

opzioni.A: Hired a resource manager.
opzioni.B: Planned strategically about timing from order to delivery to usage, managing resource risks and responses.
opzioni.C: Tracked inventory from arrival to integration.
opzioni.D: Sourced locally.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't address timing risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Teams needing significant materials plan timing, bulk vs storage and global logistics.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Tracking doesn't manage the risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It had to be bought overseas.

domande.spiegazione: Physical resources (PMBOK 7, p. 65).

domande.domanda: Halfway through an agile project, a significant scope change is needed because the project won't deliver its promised benefits. Contingency and management reserves are available. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take the change to the CCB.
opzioni.B: Use contingency reserves for the scope change.
opzioni.C: Review the change management plan.
opzioni.D: Reprioritize the backlog including the new scope and start on the highest priority item.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile uses backlog reprioritization instead of formal control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Contingency is for risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. In agile, changes are handled by reprioritizing the backlog.

domande.spiegazione: Changes (PMBOK 7, p. 66).

domande.domanda: You took over a project behind schedule and slightly over budget; no more funding and it must finish on time. You believe you can optimize the process. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add people and resources.
opzioni.B: Use the contingency reserve.
opzioni.C: Perform activities in parallel.
opzioni.D: Use lean methods to remove non-value-add activities and retrospectives for improvements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adds cost and complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reserves are for risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Fast tracking isn't process optimization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Lean and retrospectives optimize project processes.

domande.spiegazione: Project processes (PMBOK 7, p. 71).

domande.domanda: The PMO wants each team member to categorize and record their work and how long it takes, in addition to the work itself. They ask your advice. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to record and categorize their work.
opzioni.B: Recommend an automated reporting tool where possible, as categorizing work is non-value-add.
opzioni.C: Recommend an automated tool because recording work is value-add.
opzioni.D: Tell the team to ignore the request.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adds waste.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Respect the PMO while keeping processes efficient and effective.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Recording isn't value-add for the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't ignore the PMO.

domande.spiegazione: Project processes (PMBOK 7, p. 72).

domande.domanda: As Scrum master, a functional manager who knows some developers approaches them directly to add a feature to the current sprint. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Adjust the sprint backlog for the feature.
opzioni.B: Adjust the product backlog with the requirement.
opzioni.C: Ask the manager to speak with the product owner, then protect the team from direct requests.
opzioni.D: Ask the manager for a change request.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The PO prioritizes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The PO decides what goes in.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Protect team focus; the PO is the single point of prioritization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not agile.

domande.spiegazione: Maintain project team focus (PMBOK 7, p. 73).

domande.domanda: While the detailed communications plan is being signed off, you receive many ad hoc information requests from new stakeholders. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the communications management plan to include the stakeholders, their information needs and preferences.
opzioni.B: Create an information radiator for them to pull.
opzioni.C: Ignore the requests.
opzioni.D: Ask the new stakeholders to review the plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Many ad hoc requests mean planning didn't meet needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but the plan needs updating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Never ignore.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's our job to update it.

domande.spiegazione: Project communications and engagement (PMBOK 7, p. 72).

domande.domanda: Make-or-buy showed $700,000 to make vs $500,000 to buy a smart-home system. You prepare to buy. What will you do before conducting the procurement?

opzioni.A: Complete as much in-house as possible.
opzioni.B: Work with contracting professionals to develop the RFP, statement of work and terms and conditions.
opzioni.C: Add the vendor to the stakeholder register and scope to the WBS dictionary.
opzioni.D: Develop an RMP, SMP and list of resources with the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You decided to buy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. PM and technical team work with contracting professionals on bid documents.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wrong order.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor.

domande.spiegazione: Working with procurements (PMBOK 7, p. 74).
domande.nota: Option D seems invented as a distractor.

domande.domanda: A missing, not complex item, readily available from various sources, must be procured. You're ready for source selection. What will you do before sending bid documents?

opzioni.A: Prepare an RFP.
opzioni.B: Prepare an RFQ.
opzioni.C: Prepare an RFI to gather information and viable sources from the market.
opzioni.D: Review the procurement management plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. RFP is itself a bid document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. RFQ is itself a bid document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. RFI gathers market information before sending bid documents.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Decent, but RFI comes first.

domande.spiegazione: The bid process (PMBOK 7, p. 75).

domande.domanda: Part of the work is planned upfront and part is subject to change. The vendor fears confusion between pre-planned and changeable work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use a firm fixed price contract.
opzioni.B: Use a time and materials contract.
opzioni.C: Adjust the plan to be only predictive or only adaptive.
opzioni.D: Use a master agreement with the adaptive work in an appendix.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fixes scope and price.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't separate the two parts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project needs both.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Changes to adaptive scope happen without affecting the overall contract.

domande.spiegazione: Contracting (PMBOK 7, p. 76).

domande.domanda: In an agile team with very different product knowledge levels, the Scrum master suggests learning by osmosis, since information is lost in email. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Co-locate the team to capture each person's tacit knowledge.
opzioni.B: Use OPAs to capture explicit knowledge.
opzioni.C: Use the knowledge management system for explicit knowledge.
opzioni.D: Create a process to capture tacit knowledge.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Co-location captures tacit knowledge from surroundings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Explicit, not osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Explicit, not osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Co-location is the way.

domande.spiegazione: Explicit and tacit knowledge (PMBOK 7, p. 77).

domande.domanda: As product owner, you've placed high-level information in the backlog. Senior users can't articulate their requirements and fear the product won't meet their needs. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the highest priority item.
opzioni.B: Create mock-ups and prototypes with the customer.
opzioni.C: Ask for change requests.
opzioni.D: Break the work into user stories.

domande.hint: 'I'll know it when I see it'.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Requirements unclear.
